U08_bootstrap.unit: U08 bootstrap engine (wooldid_bootctl, wooldid_bootrun, wooldid_bootwire, wooldid_bootjnt, wooldid_bootcellsx, wooldid_bootsave, wooldid_isub, Mata boot kernels) on sha 8965f20

findings.title: reps() resolution caution is nested inside the cluster() block and never fires on an unclustered bootstrap
findings.claim: The resolution caution that names the p-value grid when reps() is too small to reject at 5% is emitted only when cluster() was given. The `if reps>0 { ... }` block that prints it sits inside `if "`clus'" != "" {`, so every unclustered bootstrap (standard, bayes and boottstat alike) at reps(10) runs silently. The help (367-370) promises the caution 'whenever it exceeds .05' and the code comment above the block says it was placed 'above the other bootstrap cautions', i.e. meant for every run.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 6923 opens `if "`clus'" != "" {`, 6936-6941 is the reps block, 6948 closes the clus block (awk brace-depth count over 6906-6945). u08.log B1a (att robust bootstrap(standard) reps(10)), B1b (bayes reps(10)), B1c (boottstat reps(10)): no 'grid of'/'smallest studentized' fragment; B1d (same with cluster(unit)) prints 'fall on a grid of 0.200 (2/reps)'. test_bootstrap_gates G39 (1227-1270) pins the caution on four legs, all with cluster(unit). The placement comment at 6933-6935 still justifies the block's position by 'the boottstat nesting check', which T2/T3 (456f636) deleted - the block was stranded inside the cluster() block when the code around it moved.
findings.proposed_change: Move the `if `reps' > 0 { ... }` block (6933-6941) below the closing brace at 6948 so it runs after the two-cluster refusal on every bootstrap run. Blast radius: one caution's firing condition; no number moves. Add an unclustered leg to G39.

findings.title: one straddling unit puts every unit under the keep-i rule; a per-unit rule is a small generalisation
findings.claim: The physical re-id leg decides nesting once per run: if any i value spans two cluster() values, wdb_nest=0 and no drawn copy of any cluster gets fresh unit codes, so att_i/att_it/att_itime lose the composition variance for every unit, not just the straddler. The code comment acknowledges the shape ('one straddling i out of ninety-six puts the other ninety-five under the keep-i rule') and records the author's ruling to disclose rather than handle it. The disclosure caution also fires on att-only boottstat runs, where it names estimands the run does not carry.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 9530-9560 (wdb_nest = assert min==max over ALL units; wdb_nstrad counted then dropped), 9943-9944 (`if wdb_nest gegen __wdbnewi = group(__wdbns i)` else `= i`). u08.log B3a: 24 units, unit 4 switches cluster at t>4, att_i cluster(cs): e(boot_reid)=0, e(boot_nstraddle)=1, caution printed. B3b: att-only + boottstat on the same data prints the same caution naming att_i, att_it and att_itime. No test reads e(boot_nstraddle) (grep over test/*.do).
findings.proposed_change: Per-unit rule in the reid leg: keep the per-unit straddle flag (wdbcmin != wdbcmax, already computed at 9548) as a tempvar carried by the frame copy; `gegen __wdbnewi = group(__wdbns i) if !flag` and give straddlers `i` offset past the group() range (e.g. maxcode + group(i)) so codes cannot collide. e(boot_reid) then needs a third state or nstraddle>0 alongside reid=1. Blast radius: bootrun's reid leg (two lines plus one tempvar) and the caution's condition; cost: one extra gegen per replication. Author previously ruled disclosure over per-unit (comment 9541-9546); separately gate the caution on a cell-weighted estimand being in the run. Also: the covariate re-keying (repopts2 via wooldid_isub) is gated on wdb_nest at bootrun 9950 and would have to apply whenever any unit is re-identified; wooldid_bootcells' remap reads __wdbnewi and i off the replication frame, so it survives a mixed regime unchanged.

findings.title: the 'cluster() at or above i' pairwise-degeneracy caution fires on every clustered boottstat subgroup run, including strictly finer clusters
findings.claim: wooldid_bootjnt prints the boottstat pairwise-contrast degeneracy caution whenever bts and clus are non-empty. The comment admits it is worded as 'the case it applies to rather than a fact about the run'. But the run does know: wooldid_bootrun computes wdb_nest (1 iff every i lies inside one cluster, i.e. cluster at or above i) and c_locals it to the shell, which has it in scope at the bootjnt call and does not pass it. The caution therefore fires on a cluster strictly finer than i, where its condition is false and its remedy ('a cluster() finer than i') is already in place.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 7955-7958 (gate `if "`bts'" != "" & "`clus'" != ""`), 9539/9559 (wdb_nest computed and c_local'd), 479 (bootjnt call without it). u08.log B4a: cluster(cfine)=unit*10+(t>4), subgroups(sg), boottstat: caution prints with e(boot_reid)=0 and e(boot_nstraddle)=24.
findings.proposed_change: Pass wdb_nest into wooldid_bootjnt (new option, one token on the call at 479) and add `& wdb_nest` to the gate at 7955, or gate on the event itself (pwtmiss > 0 | wdbsgjtblank set). Blast radius: one caution's condition; no number moves. No wording change.

findings.title: unconditional boottstat caution restates the help's description of the option
findings.claim: Every boottstat run prints a caution that explains what percentile-t inference is (se_analytic column, t_pt = b/se_analytic, ranks of the replications' t-statistics, equal-tailed interval, which tests are bootstrapped, where the kernel lives). It carries no condition, consequence or remedy; it is the bootts:tat help entry (394-402) reprinted, and the display footer already labels the columns.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 10928 (`dis as text "Caution: boottstat reports studentized (percentile-t) inference: ..."` inside `if wdbts {` with no further condition). u08.log B1c, B3b, B4a all print it.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the caution, or move its content into the display footer that the display unit owns (part(boot)); no wording proposed. Blast radius: one message; no number moves.

findings.title: few-treated-clusters caution carries mechanism and method comparison rather than condition/consequence/remedy
findings.claim: The caution printed when fewer than 6 treated resampling clusters exist explains what is implemented ('the pairs cluster bootstrap, which keeps only the replications that draw at least one treated cluster' / 'the Bayesian bootstrap, which shares the pairs cluster bootstrap's first two moments'), states that boottstat is not a cure, and names three alternatives including boottest outside wooldid. The help (360-362) already carries the condition and the remedies; the message is a paragraph of method exposition.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 9500 (the dis line, gated on r(N) < 6 treated clusters). u08.log B3a/B3b print it ('only 4 treated cluster(s) ...').
findings.proposed_change: Report only; the author writes the text. Keep the gate (r(N) < 6, keyed on treated clusters in e(sample)); no number moves.

findings.title: e(boot_novar) / e(boot_sesmall) cautions carry mechanism text and a second explanatory paragraph
findings.claim: When a replication's variance collapses, two cautions print: the first explains why it happens ('which happens when a resample draws too few distinct clusters and the model fits it exactly'), the second is a long paragraph listing every studentized object and every e() row the count is stored in. The sesmall caution adds a third with the mechanism of the studentized tail. Condition and count are the useful content; the rest is the wooldid_bootviab comment block rendered to the user.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 10233-10234 (novar pair), 10245 (sesmall). u08.log B3b prints the pair on a 6-cluster boottstat run (novar=1 of 8).
findings.proposed_change: Report only; author writes the text. Gates are sound (nnonv > 0; nsesmall > nnonv); no number moves.

findings.title: dots() below 0 is refused under bootstrap() but silently behaves as dots(0) under permute()
findings.claim: The dots() range check sits below the early `exit 0` that permute() runs take out of wooldid_bootctl, so a negative dots() is validated only when bootstrap() is on. Under permute() it passes and every `if dots > 0` test in the engine treats it as dots(0). The code comment records this. Same option, two behaviours between the sibling engines.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 6669-6683 (comment 'CAUTION: unlike rseed(), this range check was not hoisted above the permute() exit') and 6684 (the check). u08b.log B16: permute(shuffle) permreps(20) dots(-2) rc 0 with 20 completed; bootstrap(standard) reps(5) dots(-2) rc 198.
findings.proposed_change: Hoist the dots() range check next to the rseed() check above the stray-companion screen (6605-6617). Blast radius: a permute() call with a negative dots() starts refusing; nothing else changes.

findings.title: help: bootsave w_ column under bootalpha(size) is the row multiplier p_c/n_c, and e(boot_df) is absent under bootdf(normal)
findings.claim: The help says the w_ column records a cluster's 'Dirichlet weight under bootstrap(bayes)'. Under bootalpha(equal) it does; under bootalpha(size) wooldid_bootdw divides by n_c before the draw matrix is stored, so the column holds p_c/n_c and the columns of a replication do not sum to 1. Separately, the help's e() list names e(boot_df) unconditionally, but bootwire posts it only when a finite df resolves, so an unclustered run (default bootdf(normal)) has no e(boot_df).
findings.evidence: wooldid.sthlp 407-408; 1040. wooldid.ado 15308 (`if (amode == "size") P = P :/ N`), 9898-9899 (wmat row = __wdbdraw), 10939-10940 (boot_df posted inside `if wdbdf < .`). u08.log B6: bayes size bootsave rows sum to .03125 = 1/32 on every row; bayes equal rows sum to 1. u08b.log B13: unclustered run, e(boot_df) = .
findings.site: wooldid.sthlp 407-408 and 1040; wooldid_bootrun 9898; Mata wooldid_bootdw 15308; wooldid_bootwire 10939-10940
findings.proposed_change: Help text only: qualify the w_ sentence for bootalpha(size) and mark e(boot_df) as posted only when a t reference is in force. No code change; no number moves.

findings.title: bootwire comment says sqrt(diag(e(V_boot))) does not equal the printed se on runs with missing cells; wooldid_bootfin now rescales so it does
findings.claim: The comment block above the bootfin call states as a user-facing consequence that the per-column se and the listwise covariance diagonal disagree whenever any replication cell is missing, and that a hand test/lincom will not reproduce the Wald numbers. wooldid_bootfin's congruence rescale (vsc = se/sqrt(V_kk)) was added precisely to make the diagonal equal the printed se, and its own comment says so. The two comments contradict each other; a maintainer reading bootwire would remove or re-add the rescale wrongly.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 10356-10366 (the stale block) vs 15683-15702 (the rescale and its rationale). u08.log B7: printed se vs sqrt(V[1,1]) reldif 0.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the bootwire comment to say the diagonal is rescaled to the printed se and only the off-diagonal correlations are listwise. Comment only; no number moves.

findings.title: the guide's engine-comparison table still says the bootstrap re-identifies under a cluster finer than i
findings.claim: Row 'cluster() nesting i' of the bootstrap-vs-permute table reads 'The bootstrap re-identifies on the drawn cluster, so a cluster finer than i simply resamples inside the cohort.' Since T2/T3 (456f636) the leg re-identifies only where the cluster nests i; under a finer or cross-cutting cluster it keeps i whole (wdb_nest=0). The guide's own bootstrap chapter (281) and the help (362-366) describe the two-regime rule correctly; this row does not.
findings.evidence: wooldid_agent_guide.md 783 vs wooldid.ado 9943-9944 and help 362-366; u08.log B4a (finer cluster: e(boot_reid)=0) and test_bootstrap_gates G9 (keep-i under a finer cluster).
findings.proposed_change: Text only: align the row with the two-regime rule. No code; no number moves.

findings.title: no test pins the partial-straddle disclosure (e(boot_nstraddle)) or the resolution caution on an unclustered run
findings.claim: Two shapes the code explicitly handles have no test: (i) a partial straddle (one i value across two clusters among many nested ones), which is the case the run-level keep-i rule flips and the only case where e(boot_nstraddle) is informative; G9 tests the all-units-straddle regime and m12 reads e(boot_reid) only; (ii) the reps() resolution caution on an unclustered run, which is how the C1 nesting defect went unnoticed.
findings.evidence: grep 'nstraddle' over test/*.do: no hits; test_bootstrap_gates G39 1227-1270: four legs, all cluster(unit). u08.log B3a and B1a exercise both shapes.
findings.proposed_change: Add a partial-straddle leg asserting e(boot_nstraddle)==1, e(boot_reid)==0 and the caution; add an unclustered leg to G39. Test-only.

U08_bootstrap.works_fine:
No v1.3 analogue: `grep -i bootstrap` on main's wooldid.ado (301b706) returns nothing, and test/suite/ledger.csv has no bootstrap rows, which is correct for a new-only feature. Everything below was read on the pinned sha and, where marked, run in Stata on a 24-unit x 8-period staggered panel (seed/sortseed 2026; do-files and logs in the work dir).

Option screen (wooldid_bootctl): every refusal in the help's list (permute, impvalues, unconditionalse, customvce, oldsyntax, suppresssgprimaryeffects, multi-way cluster, boottstat with bayes/poisson/wald/bc/bca, bootdf(clusters)/bootdisplay(bca) without cluster, bootalpha with standard, bayes with cell-weighted estimands unless safety(off), stray companions) matches the code; the rseed() range check is correctly hoisted above the permute exit; level() has its own check on the plain path (5850) so the bootctl copy is not the only one; string cluster variables are excluded by `CLUSter(varlist numeric)` at 612; oldsyntax is gated on the normalized "1".

Sample concept on the count path (bootrun 9410-9450, 10218): user-if vs `keep if` with the same rseed gives mreldif 0 on e(bootdist) and e(b) for att+cluster standard, att+cluster bayes, att_it+cluster standard (reid, nest=1) and [aw] unclustered standard (B2a-d); the replication call carries no `if` and relies on missing basew being marked out, and that works.

Engine leg agreement: weighted count path vs the physical re-id leg agree on the att column to 5.8e-16 for [aw] and [pw] (B12); nothing in the suite pins the weighted case. The fweight count leg (unweighted unclustered boottstat) and the physical-expansion leg ([aw] unclustered boottstat) both run with 8/8 completed and e(boot_novar)=0 (B5). Under boottstat + cluster, the cluster substitution to __wdbns landed on every replication (the bootrun assert at 9968-9990 passed on all of B3b/B4a, B6a).

Nesting regime and disclosure: wdb_nest is computed on e(sample) (9530-9540); a nesting cluster gives e(boot_reid)=1 (B2c, B6a), a finer cluster gives 0 with nstraddle = every unit (B4a), a single straddler gives 0 with nstraddle=1 (B3a); the shell posts them only when reid and cluster are both on, as documented. isub: fe/controls/interactivecontrols/ccc_absorb are varlist-typed at 612 so `syntax` unabbreviates them, and only the string-typed coarsecohortcontrols is given `unab` - the matcher's token-boundary regex is right for i.unit, unit#c.t, c.x#i.unit, L.unit and leaves unitx/unit_2 alone; the m10-m13 gates pin the re-keying.

bootdf and e(V): default clusters when clustered (e(df_r)=23=N_clust-1=e(boot_df), B7) and normal when not (e(df_r)=., e(boot_stat)=z_wald, B13); the printed se equals sqrt(diag(e(V))) to reldif 0 (B7), confirming bootfin's congruence rescale; e(V) reposted via `ereturn repost` so the -1e100 sentinel survives; e(V_analytic)/e(V_es_analytic_*)/e(df_r_analytic) are preserved.

Families (Mata): percentile interval uses the bstat order-statistic rule; percentile p is the exact dual with weak inequalities and no add-one; BC z0 ranks against the rep-0 comparator with the ties half-weighting; BCa uses Efron's a from the delete-one-cluster jackknife and inverts at the null; boottp/bootpwt/cellwire studentized p uses the add-one convention with floor 2/(n+1) as the help says; the fixed-metric joint and equality tests (bootqf) recentre at the observed vector with the eigen guard; the studentized joint/adversarial statistics are computed inside the replication from its own e(V_es_*); the polarisation covariance in bootsgw is index-consistent with pwobs0/pwseacc by construction. The viability verdict (bootviab) edits nothing and only masks a copy handed to the kernels; e(bootdist_se) and bootsave carry the raw harvest.

bootsave: name rules checked at parse time (bootctl) and again in bootsave; 6 w_ columns = G with row sums G on every row incl. _rep=0 under standard, 1 under bayes equal, 1/n_c-scaled under bayes size (B6); the 10,000 cap applies to e(bootdist) only and bootsave reads the accumulators. The cell rewiring (bootcellsx) pairs accumulators by explicit names, remaps re-identified unit codes back to original i through the replication frame, blanks rather than mis-keys, and downgrades bca to bc for cells with a caution as the help says. Deferred display and plots read the rewired e(), so replay is free.
U08_bootstrap.untested: Not run, read only: the 10,000-row e(bootdist) cap (needs more than 10,000 completed replications); bootdisplay(bca) and the jackknife acceleration numerically (test_bootstrap_df T6d covers the surface); e(boot_V_shortfall) firing (needs many missing cells across subgroups x a long window); e(boot_covsub) numerically (gates m10-m13 cover it); poisson under bootstrap (pweight count path); gteffects/cfx cell rewiring in bootcellsx and wooldid_bootcells' remap; simultaneousbands on the bootstrap accumulator, pretrendpower after the rewire, adversarial under boottstat, and wooldid_bootsgw's polarisation numbers; the BC-withheld caution (all draws one side of the comparator); the failed-bootstrap exit path (whether e() is left analytic and replayable after r(459) from bootrun - the shell restores the observed estimate before exiting, but I did not exercise it); memory of the C x R Dirichlet draw matrix on a large unclustered bayes run (bootdw allocates it up front); the ame structural-zero blanking in bootgrab on a continuous-treatment resample; the straddle per-unit alternative itself (only the current run-level behaviour was reproduced). Dropped after review and recorded in NOTES.md with the reason: timer 100 clobbering (documented in the guide's dots() entry); e(V_es_*) not being rescaled like e(V) (a family's columns are co-present in every completed replication, so the difference cannot arise in practice); an isub abbreviation concern (the options are varlist-typed); and two error-message typos (6809 omits bca, 6885 'doe not'), which are error wording and out of scope.

U02_worker_sample.unit: U02 worker part 1: sample, onset, screens, the regression (wooldid_worker 589-1830 on 8965f20; wooldid_ifrule 5932, wooldid_anticgrid 5881, wooldid_anticesf 5899, wooldid_reltime 12780)

findings.title: Joint-test cluster caution tests i-nesting over never-treated rows, so the guide's pooled never-treated coding silences it whenever the treated i levels nest in the cluster
findings.claim: The screen at worker 1600-1651 decides 'i is nested within the cluster variable' by comparing distinct i to distinct (i, cluster) pairs over every in-sample row (1616, 1620). The help states the condition at cell level ('each treated cohort-by-period cell lies wholly inside one cluster') and only treated rows carry cell dummies, but the never-treated pool is counted too. The guide's own convention codes every never-treated unit under one i value (9999); that one code spans every cluster, so the nesting test fails and the caution is withheld exactly when the treated i levels do nest in the cluster: onset-cohort-by-stratum with cluster(stratum), or treated units as their own cohorts with cluster(unit). The sibling impvalues screen (1552-1558) restricts its identical count to targetflag == 1 for precisely this idiom, and the amescreen detect predicate (13710) tests treated cells only; the joint-test screen is the odd one out. pretrendpower() shares the gate, so both entry points to the statistic are affected.
findings.evidence: probe1.do/probe1.log on 8965f20: 8 regions x 6 units x 10 periods, onsets 5/7/never inside each region, fe(unit) cluster(region) jointtests espre(2) espost(2). i_A = cohort-by-region code for treated and 9999 for never-treated: P1a rc 0, NO caution (p1a.txt). i_B = same treated codes, never-treated 9000+region: P1b rc 0, caution 'i_B is nested within the clustering variable region' (p1b.txt line 3). The treated cell dummies and the cluster are identical between the two runs and att is bit-identical (.22651066). joint_horiz (.0447 vs .0406) and V[1,1] differ only because reghdfe's own nested-FE small-sample accounting is fooled by the 9999 code the same way (P1g in probe2.log: df_a 25 / df_a_nested 48 under i_A vs 9 / 72 under i_B) - not a different design. P1c customvce(cluster region) and P1e pretrendpower(50) on i_A are silent as well; P1d/P5d impvalues on i_A cluster(region) runs (rc 0), showing the sibling handles the idiom.
findings.site: wooldid_worker 1600-1651 (tag lines 1616 and 1620, predicate 1624); siblings wooldid_worker 1552-1558 and wooldid_amescreen 13706-13714
findings.proposed_change: Add '& `targetflag' == 1' to the two gegen tag lines at 1616 and 1620, matching the sibling at 1554/1558, so the nesting is judged on the treated event-window rows that carry cell dummies. Blast radius: the caution prints on additional runs and never on fewer; both entry points (jointtests, pretrendpower) follow since they share the gate; test_jointclus T1-T8 are unchanged because their i is nested in both domains; no e() cell moves. One consequence for the author to weigh, without proposing wording: the parenthetical '(`i' is nested within the clustering variable `jtcoarse')' would then print for an i that, taken as a whole, is not nested - under the fix it describes the treated cohorts. The more exact alternative is the amescreen cell-containment predicate (any treated (_i,_t) cell with one cluster), which would need the message reworded. Cost: two gtools tag passes restricted to fewer rows, i.e. slightly cheaper.

findings.title: The too-few-clusters guard keys on e(df_r), which ppmlhdfe never posts, so one cluster stops the reghdfe path and completes under poisson with every SE missing
findings.claim: Worker 1715 reads e(df_r) and the guard at 1723-1730 fires only when it is below 1. ppmlhdfe posts e(df_r) as missing on every run (80 clusters or 1), so under poisson the guard cannot fire: the same one-cluster input that stops the reghdfe and regress paths with 'Error: too few clusters' (459) completes under poisson with rc 0, four cautions, and every standard error missing. One cluster is a hopeless input and the run is at least loud, so this is reported for engine parity: the two paths disagree on the same data and the fix is one predicate.
findings.evidence: probe2.do/probe2.log: P4_ppmlhdfe (80 clusters) df_r=. ; P4_ppmlhdfe_onecl df_r=. N_clust=1 ; P4_reghdfe_onecl df_r=0 ; wooldid cluster(one): P4a reghdfe path rc 459 'too few clusters', P4d unconditionalse rc 459, P4b poisson rc 0 with the all-zero-VCV cautions and a table of missing SEs (probe2.log 19160-19192).
findings.proposed_change: Extend the guard's condition to '`df_r' < 1 | e(N_clust) < 2' (ppmlhdfe does post e(N_clust); on unclustered runs e(N_clust) is missing and the added clause is false). Blast radius: poisson with one cluster stops 459 like the other engines instead of completing with no variance; nothing else changes.

findings.title: An all-zero covariance prints two consecutive cautions for the same event, the first guessing at the cause
findings.claim: When e(V) comes back zero (or residue), wooldid_amescreen mode(vzero) prints a caution (13964-13968; the clustered branch at 13966 says the zero 'usually reflects a degenerate clustering' and lists remedies), and the worker then prints a second caution for the same event at 1792 whose remedy list overlaps the first. The first caution is deferred only when the cell-containment caution already printed (r1fired), so on every other vzero event the user reads two explanations of one fact, one of them speculative about the mechanism. Structural point only; which of the two survives, and its text, is the author's.
findings.evidence: probe2.log P4b (poisson, one cluster): line 'Caution: estimation returned an all-zero variance-covariance matrix. This usually reflects a degenerate clustering ...' immediately followed by 'Caution: the estimation command returned an all-zero variance-covariance matrix, so no standard error in this run is identified. ... The alternatives are (impvalues dispersion inference, bootstrap() or permute(), or a finer-than-cell clustering).' Code: wooldid_amescreen 13964-13968 prints unless r1fired == 1; wooldid_worker 1768-1792 prints whenever wdvz == 1.
findings.proposed_change: Print one caution per vzero event: either let mode(vzero) stay silent (it already returns r(vzero)/r(vzexact) for the worker's caution) or drop the worker's duplicate. Blast radius: one fewer caution line on every zero-covariance run; no e() change. Cost: nil.

findings.title: The missing-value markout strips only i./c./#, so ib#. base-level notation in controls() or fe() dies with a bare 'operator invalid' although reghdfe accepts it
findings.claim: To mark out rows with missing control values the worker rewrites the fe()/controls()/coarsecohortcontrols() text by deleting '#', 'i.' and 'c.' (752-757) and then runs 'replace ifvar = 0 if <token> >= .' on each token (769-770). A base-level spelling such as ib2.g survives the rewrite, and the replace fails inside Stata with 'ib2:  operator invalid' r(198) before estimation - no wooldid message, while the same term is legal to reghdfe. Retained v1.3 behaviour (same loop in v1.3 lines 431-438), so low; but ib#. is ordinary Stata usage and the general fix is small.
findings.evidence: probe1.log: P3a controls(ib2.g) rc 198 'ib2:  operator invalid'; P3b fe(ib2.g) rc 198 same; standalone 'reghdfe y ib2.g, absorb(i t) cluster(i)' rc 0. controls(i.g#c.x) rc 0. (coarsecohortcontrols(ib2.g) is refused earlier by validate's explicit i./c. rule at 5112-5118, a documented requirement, noted rather than reported.)
findings.proposed_change: Replace the three subinstr strips with 'fvrevar `processtemp', list' and mark out r(varlist) (the base variables of every factor/operator spelling), or strip any leading '<letters/digits>.' token per word with a regex. Blast radius: for every spelling accepted today the base-variable set is identical, so no sample or number moves; ib#./ibn./o. spellings start working. Cost: one fvrevar call per option.

findings.title: The >100-level i caution fires on every unit-level-i run and carries mechanism and modelling advice
findings.claim: Worker 1476-1478 prints, on every run whose i has more than 100 distinct values under default safety, a caution explaining that runtime grows faster than linearly in the cell count and recommending coarsening i with fe() for the units - text that is help-file material (mechanism plus modelling advice) rather than a condition-consequence-remedy for something wrong with this run. A 200-unit panel that estimates in seconds gets it every time. Author-approved as SI-8 (083ea89, 2026-08-25), so reported under the caution lens only, not as a defect; the wording is his.
findings.evidence: wooldid_worker 1476-1478 (gate si8ilev > 100 on safetyinput != off); test_si89 T3/T4 pin that it prints at 150 levels and is suppressed by safety(off).
findings.proposed_change: If anything: key the advisory on the measured cost driver (treated cell count si8cells, already computed at 1441-1443) or on a much higher level count, so a small unit-level panel is not warned every run. Blast radius: fewer prints; no e() change.

findings.title: No cert test pins the impvalues cluster screen, the pooled never-treated shape of the joint-test screen, or the one-cluster poisson path
findings.claim: test_jointclus.do T1-T8 all use a unit-level i nested in state, so the joint-test screen is never exercised on the never-treated-pooled coding the guide recommends (finding 1 would have been caught by such a case). findings.title: The analytic cfx plot-data twin leaves the user in the default frame when the write fails, with rc 0
findings.claim: The twin at shell 557-568 is `cap noi wooldid_cfxplots ... dataonly`. wooldid_cfxplots changes to a tempname frame and its `frame af { save }` fails r(602) on a file collision, so the program exits inside the tempname frame, Stata drops it and lands in `default`. The shell prints the caution and returns rc 0 but, unlike its two engine-branch siblings (269-274 and 526-531 restore `wdsh_frame'), never restores the caller's frame: a user working in a named frame is silently moved to `default`, and their next command runs on other data.
findings.evidence: u01_probe.log T4b: from frame `work` (dta_cont, 1000 rows) with u01t4_cfx.dta present and the .gph files absent, no replace: rc 0, the plot-data caution printed, `qui frame` -> FRAME=default, _N=128 (the default frame's panel), WOOLDID_LASTRC empty. T12b, the same collision in the bootstrap branch: rc 602, FRAME=work2 restored.
findings.proposed_change: Add the engine branches' restore after the twin (`qui frame` / `if r(currentframe) != wdsh_frame cap frame change wdsh_frame`). Blast radius: the shell only, no test re-bless, no number moves. Alternative with wider cover: restore `defaultframe' on every exit inside wooldid_cfxplots, which also protects the hand-call surface.

findings.title: After a complete replication loop a plot-file collision is still fatal and refuses replay; the sibling bootsave/permsave collision became a caution with a posted rc on 2026-09-21
findings.claim: In both engine blocks the deferred wooldid_esplots / wooldid_cfxplots calls propagate a graph-save r(602) as the error of the call: the whole loop has completed, e() is fully rewired, part(1)/part(2) have printed, but the part(perm)/part(boot) footer is skipped, WOOLDID_LASTRC is set so bare `wooldid` refuses, and a do-file aborts. The author's 2026-09-21 ruling turned the identical failure of the two savers, at the same post-loop position, into a caution plus e(*_save_rc). The shell's comment at 557-568 keeps the plot failure fatal because 'the same call also draws the figures', but on the realistic r(602) the figure(s) up to the collision drew (name(..., replace)) and only the file write failed; families after the failing save are not drawn, since wooldid_esplots draws and saves per family.
findings.evidence: u01_probe.log T12b (bootstrap, dta_cont, cfx .gph collision): rc 602, LASTRC=602, e(boot_method)=standard intact. u01_probe4.log T10b (permute, 20 reps, u01t10_ES_att.gph collision): tables printed, 'file u01t10_ES_att.gph already exists', rc 602, LASTRC=602, e(perm_completed)=20 and e(perm_p_att)=.0952 intact, footer absent, replay r(198). test_bootstrap_gates G20 (chk 20b 602 / 20d 198) pins the current behaviour.
findings.proposed_change: Apply the savers' ruling to the deferred plot calls: catch the rc, post it under a name the author picks, print a caution in his wording, continue to the footer and the marker clear. Blast radius: the four shell sites, optionally the worker's deferred esplots call at 4884 for the analytic path; re-bless test_bootstrap_gates G20 (20b/20d) and, if 4884 is included, test_edges E9. No number moves.

findings.title: wooldid, update re-runs the analytic plot-data write on the PREVIOUS run's e()
findings.claim: The shell's analytic cfx plot-data twin (557-568) keys on e(wdid_cfxsave), but the worker's update branch (614-618) exits rc 0 without posting e(). After any makecfxplots saveplots() run, a later `wooldid, update` therefore reaches the twin with the previous run's hidden macros and rewrites <stem>_cfx.dta from the old e(cfx*) matrices: with e(wdid_cfxrepl) set it overwrites silently, without it the plot-data caution prints about a file update never touched. The rewritten content is identical to what the file already held, so the cost is a spurious write or a spurious caution, not wrong data; the mechanism matters because any future rc-0 exit without a post hits it too.
findings.evidence: Stubbed net install (wooldid_stub.ado, one line changed to `dis "UPDATE_STUB_RAN"`). u01_probe3.log T7a rc 0 CFXSAVE=[u01t7] REPL=[replace]; erase u01t7_cfx.dta (T7b confirm rc 601); `wooldid, update` T7c rc 0; T7d confirm rc 0, the file reappeared. T7e/T7f: previous run without replace -> update prints 'file u01t7_cfx.dta already exists' and the plot-data caution. T7g: after a plain run update is clean.
findings.proposed_change: Gate the twin on THIS call having posted: have the worker c_local the stem and the replace flag beside the e() post (4766-4767) and let the shell read the locals, or compare e(cmdline) with `wooldid `0'' before firing. Blast radius: shell 557-568 plus worker 4766-4767; no test re-bless; no number moves.

findings.title: The replay-staleness marker is keyed to the session, not to the e() it protects, so it refuses two working replays
findings.claim: WOOLDID_LASTRC is set on ANY nonzero rc (128-130) and read only by the bare-line branch (40-43). Two realistic cases refuse a valid store: (1) a failed call followed by `estimates restore` of a good wooldid store, which the user selected explicitly; (2) an option typed on the replay line (`wooldid, level(90)`) falls to the worker, fails at parse with the too-few-variables error without touching e(), and still sets the marker, so the next bare `wooldid` is refused until a full refit. Both are documented as design (help 931, guide 909), so this is a generalisation candidate for the author, not a defect.
findings.evidence: u01_probe.log T3c: failed call, est restore mC1, `wooldid` -> 'Error: the last wooldid call failed; refit wooldid before replaying.' r(198). u01_probe2.log T14/T14b: `wooldid, level(90)` -> too-few-variables r(198), LASTRC=[198]; then bare `wooldid` refused. u01_probe4.log T3a/T3b: with the marker clear, replay after est restore and replay with no data both rc 0, as the guide says.
findings.proposed_change: Option A (narrow, two lines): do not set the marker when the failing `0' carries no varlist (begins with a comma); covers the replay-line typo only. Option B: mark the e() itself with a hidden macro written on failure only when e(cmd)==wooldid and e(cmdline)==`wooldid `0'' (the failed call's own post) and read that in the replay branch; a restored clean store then replays, but an estimation-stage failure of a NEW spec would no longer be refused, which the author's stated rationale wants refused, so that trade-off is his to rule. Blast radius: shell only; no number moves.

findings.title: The cfx plot-data twin's failure posts no rc, while the two savers post e(boot_save_rc)/e(perm_save_rc) precisely because a caution is invisible under quietly
findings.claim: Shell 559-566 captures the rc into wdsh_dc and prints a caution; nothing reaches e(). The savers' conversion (comment at 7059-7066; shell 300-303 and 474-476) argued that a quietly-run script has no signal but a posted rc; the same argument applies to a silently stale <stem>_cfx.dta.
findings.evidence: Reading: wooldid 559-566 has no ereturn; wooldid 300-303 and 474-476 post the saver rcs.
findings.proposed_change: Post the rc under a name the author chooses (one `ereturn local` after line 565) and document it beside e(boot_save_rc). Blast radius: shell plus one help line; no number moves.

findings.title: permute prints a >10,000 draw-cap caution (Claude draft, flagged for the author); the bootstrap twin prints and posts nothing

findings.title: The BS-15 degenerate-contrast guard is silently inert under suppresssgprimaryeffects
findings.claim: wooldid_sgdeg rebuilds the implied correlation of two subgroups' effects from the level standard errors in e(wdidsgresults_*), and those matrices are never posted under suppresssgprimaryeffects, so every row is skipped and the guard never fires. The user who asks only for the contrasts therefore receives the exact degenerate contrast (SE = cancellation residue, p of order 1e-46) that a normal run blanks under a caution, and nothing is said. The help (~645) and the guide (chapter 8) promise the blanking unconditionally; the sgdeg comment claims the inertness is 'documented in the help', which it is not.
findings.evidence: run_a2.log a14 vs run_a3.log a19/a20 on test/data/dta_binary: `att cluster(i) subgroups(sg) esprelength(2) espostlength(2)`. Normal run: e(pwsgs) att:2vs1 est .07034906 se . p ., e(joint_att_allsgssame) = ., e(wdid_sgdegen)=2 (rho .9993, act blank), caution printed. Same call + suppresssgprimaryeffects: est .07034906 se .0022844 t 30.8 p 9.16e-46, e(joint_att_allsgssame) 9.16e-46, e(wdid_sgdegen) empty, NO caution. robust twin: se .1002352 p .48 (the clustered contrast se is 1/44 of it, the same ratio test_sgdegen measures). v1.3 reports the same unguarded numbers under suppresssgprimaryeffects (the guard is new-only), so a dual-build comparison is IDENTICAL there and the ledger has nothing to say; the suite's only suppresssgprimaryeffects config (ext_cov10_suppress_sg) is robust.
findings.site: wooldid_worker 4853 (call gate); wooldid_sgdeg 11891-11892 (cap confirm e(wdidsgresults_`sg') -> continue); the level SEs the polarisation needs are returned by the pwcompare pass itself at 3337 / 3391 (r(table)) but are only kept under the EFF3 flags set at 3061 / 3119, which are inside the suppresssgprimaryeffects-gated block at 3050
findings.proposed_change: Under suppresssgprimaryeffects keep the level SEs the pwcompare pass already returns in r(table) (the EFF3 read at 3352-3359 / 3440-3447, today gated on sgeff3_ flags that are never set when the level block is skipped) in a hidden matrix, and let wooldid_sgdeg read that when e(wdidsgresults_*) is absent. Blast radius: suppresssgprimaryeffects on the analytic path only; cost one matrix copy per estimand. Add a cluster(i) suppresssgprimaryeffects leg to test_sgdegen.

findings.title: E1b's jointmarginsdof is threaded into the binary whole-sample joint tests only
findings.claim: The E1b comment (2229-2236) argues the pre-trend joint tests cannot take marginsdof because it becomes nose under impvalues/fastnose, and builds jointmarginsdof for the two binary whole-sample sites. findings.title: 8-digit subgroup values: sgdom cautions before estimation, then the finished run dies r(198) building a result name
findings.claim: wooldid_sgdom already computes the longest subgroup value and lists in its own comment the three name templates that overflow at 8 digits, yet it only cautions. For the option sets those templates belong to (att_itime with a pre-window; adversarial with esfixedbaseperiod), the crash is certain and arrives after the regression and after the tables print, so the finished run is thrown away. The predicate (longest value + the requested options) is fully known before estimation.
findings.evidence: probe1.log P5A: caution printed, 'Wooldid is now estimating its regression.' printed, then 'pretreatment_SG10000001_att_itime invalid name' r(198). P5C: tables printed, then 'adversarial_pval_att_it_s10000001 invalid name' r(198). P5B (9 digits, att only) rc 0. Code: wooldid_sgdom 13131-13146 (caution, comment naming the templates); worker 4364 (rownamespool_sginj = ..._SG`sgcase'_) and 4721-4722 (ereturn scalar/matrix adversarial_*_s`sgcase').
findings.proposed_change: Lead with a conditional handling that needs no new error wording: in wooldid_sgdom compute the exact worst-case name length for the requested options (the prefix table its own comment lists plus the digit count) and, only when it exceeds 32, recode the subgroup values to a dense index for the run (keeping a value map for labels). Because the predicate fires only where the run would have crashed after estimation, it has zero blast radius on runs that work today and moves no numbers. Fallback: refuse before the regression on the same predicate (wording the author's), keeping the caution for option sets that merely might overflow.

findings.title: i above 2,147,483,647 passes validate's assert and dies late with Stata's misleading 'noninteger values' message
findings.claim: wooldid_reltime builds _i from the raw i codes (gen double _i = i), and i._i#i._t#i.targetflag is a factor variable, so i is bounded by Stata's factor-variable level cap. validate's assert checks positivity and integrality only. A 10-digit integer id (common administrative id width) therefore reaches the regression and fails r(452) '__000005: factor variables may not contain noninteger values' - a tempvar name and a wrong diagnosis. wooldid already names this cap for subgroup values (sgdom caution) but not for i, which is the more likely place for a large id.
findings.evidence: probe1.log P4A/P4B (i = 3,000,000,001..): r(452) with the noninteger message, same under safety(off). probe3.log Q7A (i = 2,147,483,001..) rc 0; Q7B (i = 2,147,483,649..) r(452). Code: wooldid_validate 5340-5346 (assert i > 0 & int(i) == i); wooldid_reltime 12963; sgdom caution 13146 names the cap for subgroups.
findings.proposed_change: The cap is a Stata hard limit, not a risk the user can accept, so whichever fix is taken must sit OUTSIDE the safety() gate (P4B shows safety(off) dies identically). Lead with the general handling: when max(i) on the estimation sample exceeds 2,147,483,647, build _i in wooldid_reltime as a dense group index of i (egen group), keeping i's original code for anything that labels cohorts (the histogram is by _i level; att_i/att_itime are aggregates). findings.title: customvce() is held out of the default cell collapse 'pending measurement'; measured, it is as exact as cluster()

The collapse's exactness argument (the treatment derivative is cell-constant and margins reads only e(b)/e(V)) does not depend on which command produced e(V); on the plain reg/poisson path with vce(cluster) or vce(robust) there is no row-count check of the kind that makes unconditionalse ineligible. With the exclusion removed on a patched copy, the collapsed and uncollapsed customvce() runs agree to the same 1e-16 class as the already-eligible cluster() path, on binary, weighted, event-study, joint-test, subgroup and poisson configurations.

findings.title: cfxplotnose: permute() keeps the 6-column cfx shape and fills it from replications; bootstrap() truncates to 1 column and the cell rewiring skips it

findings.title: Fast mode keeps the full delta-method VCE on the binary subgroup-by-horizon call while the continuous twin synthesizes the estimability marker

findings.title: Analytic simultaneous band is simulated from a normal law while the pointwise intervals it is drawn over use t(df_r): with few clusters the band is narrower than the pointwise interval and under-covers
findings.claim: wooldid_esbanda draws z ~ N(0,R) and takes the level() quantile of max|z|, with no degrees of freedom, while the table's pointwise interval comes from margins with df(df_r). At small df_r the sup-t normal critical value falls below the t quantile for two horizons, so the dashed simultaneous band sits inside the pointwise shading it is supposed to widen, and for four horizons its simultaneous coverage under the package's own t convention is 88% at nominal 95%. The help says the band covers every horizon at level() and the guide table says it is calibrated always; the bootstrap engine was fixed for exactly this symptom (B9) and the analytic one was not.
findings.evidence: probe1.log P2: 3-cohort i, fe(unit) cluster(unit), df_r=9, horizons pre2/post0: e(esband_crit_att)=2.21188 < invttail(9,.025)=2.26216, so the band half-width on pre2 is 0.848 against the printed pointwise 0.868. P2b (4 horizons, df_r=9): engine crit 2.4555 (200k-draw normal-law hand value 2.484); sup-t crit under a t(9) law 3.027; simultaneous coverage of the engine band under the t(9) law 0.880. Pointwise interval built with marginsdof df(df_r) at worker 2213. test_esband B2 floors the crit at invnormal(.975) on a 24-cluster fixture where the gap cannot show; B9's never-narrower check runs only under boottstat.
findings.site: wooldid_esbanda 17835-17897 (rnormal draws, no df argument); wooldid_esband 11640-11745 analytic branch (no dfr()); worker 4635 call; help 297-301; guide table line 423 ('not calibrated when: none')
findings.proposed_change: Pass df_r into wooldid_esbanda and, when it is finite, divide each draw column's max|z| by sqrt(rchi2(df)/df) (multivariate-t sup); the band is then never narrower than the t pointwise interval and covers at level() under the package's own t convention. Applies ONLY to the analytic branch of wooldid_esband (the kernel called from worker 4635 with a finite df_r); the bootstrap engine is a percentile-t over draws with no distributional law and is untouched. Blast radius: kernel signature, one call site in wooldid_esband (new dfr()), worker 4635 passes df_r, test_esband B2's floor becomes invttail(df,.025); analytic e(esband_*) baselines re-bless.

findings.title: pretrendpower() NIS pre-test uses a t(df_r) critical value inside a normal-law quadrature, so the reported '5%' pre-test size is the size of no test wooldid or Roth runs (2.4% at df 9, k=1); BS-11 ('pin the pre-test at five percent') is half-implemented
findings.claim: ptpniscrit is invttail(dfr, .025) but the rejection probability, the reported size and the mdt_nis bisection are all evaluated with mvnormalcvqp under a normal law. The resulting e(roth_nissize_*) is P(|Z| > t_{df,.975}), which is neither the 5% of Roth's pretrends convention (normal critical value, normal law) nor the 5% of the t-law test wooldid's own pointwise columns run. mdt_nis and bias_nis are solved against that hybrid curve, so they do not power either test at the stated 5%, contradicting the help ('both at the 5% level') and the code comment claiming the two detectable-trend columns are at one size.
findings.evidence: probe1.log P1: df_r=9, k=1: e(roth_nissize_att)=0.02368769, equal to 2*(1-normal(invttail(9,.025))) exactly, not 0.05. P1b (k=2, df 9): reported size 0.04679; the normal-critical-value size on the same block (hand mvnormalcvqp) is 0.09745. The pretrends crosscheck (test/suite/newfeat/pretrends_crosscheck.do) records the package's implied size against e(roth_nissize_att) as info only, and test_level L12 pins .07961397 without asking which law it is the size under.
findings.site: wooldid_ptp 11097-11098 (ptpniscrit = invttail(dfr,(100-95)/200)) with the mvnormalcvqp calls at 11296, 11330, 11342, 11351; help 569-572; guide 453; commit 5f5dc6c (BS-11)
findings.proposed_change: Three routes, the ruled BS-11 text names no law so the author picks: (a) invnormal(1-(100-95)/200) for ptpniscrit, one line, exactly Roth's convention and the normal law already in use; (b) keep the t threshold and make the law t as well by mixing the quadrature over the chi2: for a few dozen draws of sqrt(rchi2(df)/df) call mvnormalcvqp with the sd vector scaled by that factor and average, about 30x the present cost, no rewrite, and the only route under which 5% is the size of the test wooldid's own pointwise columns run; (c) the full t-law integration. Any route moves e(roth_nissize_*), mdt_nis and bias_nis on every run with finite df_r (test_level L12's pinned nissize moves); mdt_wald, the slope and its CI do not.

The author's d77a726 campaign measured the bootstrapped adversarial statistic on exactly that geometry as rejecting nothing under the null and nothing under a step violation the analytic test detects at p=1e-9, and concluded it carries no information. Neither document absorbed that, and wooldid_bootjnt computes and posts the p under boottstat with no containment check or caution.

findings.title: The pretrendpower() rank-deficiency follow-up caution carries the singleton-cell mechanism (zero treated residuals, sandwich algebra, proportional weight vectors) rather than condition, consequence and remedy
findings.claim: After the rank-deficient caution, wooldid_ptp prints a second, longer line when the largest treated cell holds one observation. It states the condition (cellmax == 1), the consequence and the remedies (coarser i with fe(), bootstrap() or permute()), but wraps them in an explanation of why the residuals vanish and how the covariance is built from control-cell variation, which is help text the caution already cites by section.
findings.evidence: wooldid_ptp 11255 in full: 'The usual cause is a singleton-cell design, and this run is one: every treated (i, relative-period) cell holds exactly one observation, so the treated residuals are identically zero and this covariance is built from control-cell variation alone - two pre-period horizons can then be reported as exactly proportional when their estimates are not. It is not caused by the clustering, and it is present under robust. A coarser i (cohorts, or treatment-onset groups) with unit fixed effects supplied through fe() removes it, and bootstrap() or permute() give inference that does not read this matrix. See the Design conditions for every consumer of e(V_es_*) in the help, condition Two.' Line 11256 is the multi-observation twin with the same shape.
findings.site: wooldid_ptp 11254-11258 (the rank-deficient caution and its two conditional follow-ups); guide messages chapter line 1044

findings.title: mdt_nis and the NIS size are omitted above 4 pre-periods on cost grounds; a fixed-seed Monte-Carlo evaluator, which the analytic band already uses, would handle any k
findings.claim: wooldid_ptp caps the exact mvnormalcvqp quadrature at k <= 4 and sends larger designs to Roth's package for the column. Long pre-histories (esprelength(5) or more) are ordinary in staggered panels. The NIS rejection probability at slope g is P(max_j |z_j + g m_j/sd_j| > c) over a correlated normal vector, the same object wooldid_esbanda evaluates by 10,000 fixed-seed draws in milliseconds; a Monte-Carlo evaluator with the same seed-save/restore lifts the cap without touching the k <= 4 numbers if it is used only above 4.
findings.evidence: wooldid_ptp 11289-11293: 'exact quadrature cost explodes with dimension (~2.9s per evaluation at k=6, ~85 evaluations per power level per type); cap the NIS column at k <= 4'; help 573-574 and guide 453 document the omission. wooldid_esbanda 17835-17897 is the existing MC sup evaluator with the RNG discipline in wooldid_esband 11662-11723.
findings.site: wooldid_ptp 11289-11293 and the bisection 11322-11360; help 573-574; guide 453

Blast radius: wooldid_ptp NIS block only; fills cells that are missing today and moves nothing that is reported.

findings.title: Under permute() without permstrata() the subgroup-equality test and the pairwise contrast of the same two subgroups print p = 1.000 and p = 0.010 on one run; the pairwise row's off-centre flag is set internally but never reported, with or without strata
findings.claim: With subgroups() at the cluster level, a nonzero common effect and no permstrata(), the shuffle's null draws of the subgroup att and of the contrast are centred away from zero: permwire names main_SG1_att and blanks its interval. The pairwise kernel also flags the contrast off-centre (kernel row 10 = 1) and blanks its interval, but the contrast row is named in no caution and not in e(perm_offcentre), and its p (.0103) prints as a test of 1 vs 0. The equality test on the same two subgroups ranks the uncentred W_r = d_r^2/s^2 against W_obs; every W_r exceeds W_obs (min 5.467 > 4.689) and p = 1.000 prints under 'p-value for joint test that all SGs have the same att'. The analytic run on the same data gives one p for both (8.3e-6), as two subgroups require; with the sharp null true (effect 0) the permutation pair agree (.072 vs .144, the absolute-vs-equal-tailed gap). With the engine's own remedy permstrata(sg) the pair are .89 vs .31 and the pairwise row is still flagged internally and still unreported while the caution lists all eight e(b) columns. The footer says the adversarial p tests the sharp null rather than the composite null; the contrasts and the equality test carry no such statement.

findings.title: esttab reports the permutation p-values under the fast-mode default but the ANALYTIC p-values under permanalyticse and permtstat, against the help's 'p-values and intervals remain permutation-based'
findings.claim: The e(p)/e(ci_l)/e(ci_u) posting for estout is gated on e(V) being absent. Under permanalyticse (and permtstat) e(V) is the analytic covariance, so estout derives p and CI from b and V: esttab printed main_att p = 0.0000 *** while the run's own table carried p_perm = .0328 and the header says randomization inference; under permtstat esttab printed 3e-06 against a table p_perm of .095. Under the fast-mode default the same esttab call printed the permutation p (.0328 *). The code comment says this is deliberate ('the tools already work from it'), but an exported coefficient table silently changes inference family with an option whose help says the p-values stay permutation-based.

U07_permute.works_fine: Examined and found sound (all on the pinned copy, Stata 19 MP, seeds and sortseeds set; logs in the work dir): (1) the shuffle generator, sampled and exact: on a 6-cluster {5,5,7,.,.,.} design permexact enumerates M = 60 distinct assignments, every column keeps the observed multiset, the observed assignment is found (e(perm_addone) empty) and p_att sits at the exact floor 2/60; (2) permstrata() with cluster order crossing stratum order (st = mod(i,2)+1): M = 4 x 6 = 24, and every enumerated and sampled replication preserves the within-stratum multisets read back from permsave's onset_* columns, so the __wdprow key does what its comment says; (3) permute(probabilities) row mapping with clusters listed in descending order and deterministic rows: onset_6 == 5 in 40/40 draws, onset_2 missing in 40/40, a .5/.5 cluster at 19/40; (4) the p-value convention: a by-hand equal-tailed add-one p recomputed from e(permdist_b) and e(perm_comparator_b) matches e(perm_p) for every column, and e(perm_comparator_b) equals e(b) bitwise under the fast-mode default; (5) permonsetcohorts: with i = onset grouping and cluster = unit, three replications rebuilt BY HAND from permsave's assignment row (onsets to units, icoh from onsets, fastnose refit) reproduce the saved coefficient rows bitwise, so the rebuild map is right end-to-end and the rep-0 identity assertion is a live check; (6) permtstat with cluster(st) coarser than i and an event-study window: comparator b == e(b), comparator se == e(perm_ase_obs), the se column == the hidden analytic twin, t_perm == b/se, all bitwise; the vsplice skip in rep mode does not touch the diagonal; (7) a messy unbalanced state/county panel (8% rows dropped, early periods removed for some counties, 3% missing y) with subgroups(): 40/40 replications, no blanks, subgroup equality and pairwise surfaces rewired; aw weights alone and [aw] with an if-restriction both run; (8) a replication in which a subgroup has no treated cluster does NOT fail: the plain run accepts it (rc 0), and in 120 replications the 26 such assignments kept the pooled draw and blanked only the subgroup columns (e(perm_n) = 94 for SG1), which disproved my failure-path hypothesis; (9) rows with a missing cluster() value are marked out of the estimation sample by the worker itself (line 761-771), independent of fastnose, so the design-sample sentinel never reaches an estimated row as permrun claims; (10) level(90) renames the interval columns lb_90ci/ub_90ci; permstepdown's adjusted p is monotone in |t_obs| and >= p_raw; the adversarial and joint pre-trend permutation p's post under esfixedbaseperiod; e(perm_precaveat) = 1; (11) the bare `wooldid` replay after a permute run reprints at rc 0; (12) the guide's claim that customvce() is refused holds (via the wrong branch, finding 5). Help claims checked against code and found consistent: the 65,534 enumeration ceiling and the 10,000 posting cap, the max(20, half) completion floor, the < 6 ever-treated caution, the 2/(permreps+1) floor caution, permtci implying permtstat, the permsave layout (rep 0 row, onset_* columns), the extended-missing refusal, the no-single-assignment refusal.

findings.title: amescreen detect treats a one-row treated cell as cluster containment and withholds every ame standard error, unliftably
findings.claim: The detect predicate fires when ANY treated cohort-by-period cell of the estimation sample holds a single distinct cluster value. A cell that holds a single ROW (i coarser than unit, cluster(unit) finer than i, and an unbalanced panel where a cohort thins to one unit in some period) satisfies that with nunique = 1, so the whole run's ame inference is scrubbed and e(V_es_ame*) withheld, with no safety() escape. But a one-row cell carrying its own intercept is fit exactly: its residual and score are zero, so it cannot contaminate the cluster-robust meat, and its dose slope is dropped for collinearity anyway. The scrub throws away valid inference on exactly the design the help recommends as the containment remedy (a cluster() strictly finer than the cells).
findings.evidence: wooldid_amescreen mode detect 13710-13716 (gegen nunique by (icell tcell) if esamp & tflag==1; tag on amecl == 1; fire if any). Consumers of amescrub at 2567, 2622, 2780, 2913, 3496 ... carry no safety gate. Stata P1-A (s1_probes.log 19003-19078): 30 cohorts x 6 units, cluster(unitid), cohort 2 reduced to one unit at t=9 -> 'Caution: ... 1 treated i-t cell(s) lie completely within a single cluster', 7 of 14 SEs not identified, e(V_es_ame) absent (rc 111); identical under safety(off) (19090-19158). P1-B with that single row deleted: no fire, e(V_es_ame) posted. P1-C on a scratch copy with amescrub forced 0 (s2_probes.log 19051-19074): the withheld SEs agree with P1-B to 3.1e-4 on every ES_ame horizon (post0 .189323 vs .189264, pre3 .211433 vs .211367, ...) and pretreatment:ame (.120259 vs .120222); the att SEs move by the same 3e-4, i.e. the (N-1)/(N-K) factor from one row and one column; ES_ame point estimates identical to 6 digits. test_amescreen A4 covers multi-row partial containment (refA.dta, cmix) and never a one-row cell.
findings.site: wooldid_amescreen 13703-13723 (mode detect), caller wooldid_worker 1749-1755; binary sibling's one-row shape at wooldid_worker 2044 (gtnob <= 1)
findings.proposed_change: In mode detect, count rows per cell on the same domain (one gegen total by (icell tcell) if esamp & tflag == 1, the shape wooldid_worker 1999 already uses for gtnob) and tag only cells with nunique == 1 AND rows >= 2. Outside lattice() the excluded one-row cells are already announced by the interaction-drop caution (its display is gated on lattice == "" | verbose at 12718, so under a lattice with verbose off they would be silent, as they are today). This does not conflict with the gteffects cluster-mode count at 2029-2035, which deliberately counts one-row cells: that disclosure is about the cell's OWN standard error, which is genuinely understated, whereas detect asks whether the aggregate ame covariance is contaminated, which for a zero-score row it is not. Blast radius: runs whose only contained cells are one-row cells stop firing, so their ame se/t/p/ci, e(V_es_ame*) and ame joint/adversarial tests go from missing to reported; every multi-row containment (cluster at or above i, the suite's cont_* configs whose v1.3 ame SEs were real numbers, refA) fires exactly as today. Cost: one extra gegen pass, only under contreat() with a cluster-type VCE.

findings.title: The dose-slope (amevoid) screen never runs under contreatwithin, so the ame rows print structural zeros with no caution naming them
findings.claim: wooldid_validate rewrites the working safety value to off whenever contreatwithin accompanies contreat(), and the ccscreen call is gated on that working value. The relaxation exists for the dropped-DUMMY error (periods without a control group), but it also switches off the two screens that never refuse - the every-dose-slope-dropped void and the interactivecontrols twin. The contreatwithin user is precisely the one reading ame, and the finest-i design the guide warns about (i = unit, one row per cell) drops every slope: the run then reports ame = 0 on every row, standard errors missing, and nothing says the zeros are structural. Guide sec 12 documents the behaviour, but documenting it does not make the output readable.
findings.evidence: wooldid_validate 5199 (local safety off under contreatwithin + contreat); wooldid_worker 1955 (if "`safety'" != "off" wooldid_ccscreen ...); wooldid_ccscreen 12751-12762 (amevoid) and 12768 (icscreen) sit inside that call. Stata P4R (s3_probes.log 18958-19001): i = unit, contreat(dose) contreatcontrols(basic) contreatwithin robust -> rc 0, main:ame = 0, pretreatment:ame = 0, every ES_ame horizon = 0, SEs missing; the only cautions are the generic 'standard errors were not identified for 6 of 12' and 'no horizon of the ame event study has an identified variance'. Same data without contreatwithin (19025-19075): the dose-slope caution prints and the ame rows are missing. Same pattern under cluster(i) (s1_probes.log 19477-19665). Help 664-665 promises 'under default safety wooldid names this situation' with no contreatwithin carve-out; the help's contreatwithin passage (796-801) does not mention it either.
findings.proposed_change: Gate the ccscreen CALL on safetyinput (the user's own value) and pass the working value in as an option; inside ccscreen keep the dropped-dummy loop (12592-12735, the error 322 path) on the working value, and run the amevoid block and the icscreen call whenever the user's own value is not off. Blast radius: contreatwithin runs in which every dose slope dropped - their ame point cells go from 0 to missing with the caution, and the interactive-control caution can newly print under contreatwithin; explicit safety(off) skips everything as today. The only numbers moved are structural zeros. Suite footprint: real_cont_within (configs.csv, dose_it varies within cohort) and 39 configs_ext.csv rows (the ext_c1_h* grid, ext_val_within_bytime_safety, ext_char_within_bytime_off, ext_cov10_cont_within_vary) carry contreatwithin; a config moves only if every treated-cell dose slope is dropped there, which would show today as an all-zero ame column - the ledger records real ame numbers for the cont_* family, so the expected battery movement is none, to be confirmed by a dual-build run.

findings.title: An all-zero covariance prints two cautions for one event, and the amescreen copy carries mechanism text
findings.claim: wooldid_amescreen mode vzero prints its own three-variant caution whenever the residue floor fires and the containment caution did not, and the worker then prints a second caution for the same detection. On a run that trips it, five cautions follow one event: amescreen's, the worker's, the 'n of n standard errors not identified' line and the two event-study covariance lines. The two vzero texts give the remedies in different orders (amescreen: 'bootstrap SEs, IM p-values, or randomization inference'; worker: 'bootstrap() or permute() ... impvalues ... finer-than-cell clustering'). The amescreen variants also explain Stata's internals ('Stata replaces a variance matrix it judges nonsymmetric or highly singular with zeros, which is what a near-singular design does to the sandwich estimator') and, on the residue case, the order of the noise and of the p-values - help text rather than condition, consequence and remedy.
findings.evidence: wooldid_amescreen 13960-13964 (three dis as text under `vzero' & r1fired != 1); wooldid_worker 1764-1792 (second caution under wdvz == 1, unconditional). Stata P6 (s2_probes.log 19164-19174): contreat(dose) contreatcontrols(basic) lattice(byCohort 3) robust -> line 19164 'Caution: estimation returned an all-zero variance-covariance matrix. Nothing in this run was clustered...' then 19168 'Caution: the estimation command returned an all-zero variance-covariance matrix, so no standard error in this run is identified...' then 19170, 19172, 19174. Guide messages chapter lists both families (935 and 1077-1079). test_amescreen A5 scans only for the worker's text.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the detection in amescreen (r(vzero), r(vzexact)) and print from ONE site. The two texts are not nested: the worker's block (1775-1792) carries the per-case noun and the cluster/robust/customvce remedy branching, while only amescreen's third variant (13964, via latflag) carries the lattice steer ('With lattice() the usual cause is treated cohort-by-period cells that hold too few distinct values...') - and the reproduced run P6 is a lattice run. So which text survives, and whether the lattice sentence migrates into the surviving site, is the author's call; the structural request is one caution per event. Blast radius: message count only; no number moves.

findings.title: The within-cell subgroup guard W1 is a strict subset of the split-unit guard S1 with the identical error; under safety(off) a within-cell violation gets S1's over-time caution
findings.claim: A subgroup varying within an (i,t) cell necessarily varies within i, so every run W1 refuses is one S1 would refuse on the next assert, with the same rc 459 and the byte-identical error string. Under default safety W1 therefore buys nothing observable; under safety(off) W1 is skipped and the within-cell case falls through to S1's caution, which describes a different defect (a unit splitting over time) and states a consequence that is wrong for this case ('by-subgroup att and att_it results are unaffected' - within-cell variation is exactly what makes those contrasts structurally unable to show heterogeneity, the reason W1 exists per its own comment at 13024-13031). W1 costs two gegen passes by (i t) plus an assert on every subgroups() run and every replication. This is input to the HELD ruling R-B on hardening S1/S2.
findings.evidence: wooldid_sgdom 13033-13057 (W1: gegen min/max by (i t), assert, error text) and 13060-13073 (S1: by (i), same error text at 13069, caution at 13072). Stata P2 (s1_probes.log 19303-19433): sg = mod(unit,2)+1 inside 6-unit cohorts; default -> rc 459 with the 13054 text; safety(off) -> rc 0 and 'Caution: the subgroup variable sg splits some units of i across multiple subgroups over time; proceeding under safety(off) using share weighting...'. review_process/open_ticket_sgshareweight_2026-09-21.md and changes_review_2026-09-22.md line 33 (R-B HELD).
findings.proposed_change: Two shapes, for the author to choose with R-B: (a) delete W1 - nothing observable changes under default safety and the two by-(i t) passes go; or (b) keep W1 and let it fire under safety(off) too (as a caution with its own consequence), so the within-cell case is no longer described as a time split. Either way, no number moves; (b) changes which caution prints on scr_sgsplit_off-like runs only if their subgroup varies within a cell (the suite's sgstr_straddle is a time split, so it would not).

findings.title: bycoh cautions on a near-unidentified reference pool (sd between 1e-5 and 1e-3 of the sample sd); ccref has no such band and runs silently there
findings.claim: The two reference-pool screens share the 1e-5 relative refusal cut, and the bycoh header says they 'move together by construction'. That holds for the refusal only: bycoh adds a fragility caution when a cohort's reference-pool sd lies in (1e-5, 1e-3) of the sample sd, warning that the cohort's baseline slope is nearly unidentified and regtol() does not reach it; ccref's per-type loop has no caution arm, so a byTtre onset group, a byTreated arm, a byTime calendar period or the whole basic pool sitting in that same band runs with no message. A thin late-period never-treated pool under byTime is the realistic trigger. This is the false-negative side of the sibling pair.
findings.evidence: wooldid_amescreen 13767-13796 (ccref loop: the only test is ccrng < 2 | ccrsdg >= . | ccrsdg <= ccrtol*ccrsd, then fail/continue; no band) vs 13858-13868 (bycoh: count if bcsd > 1e-5*bcsamp & bcsd < 1e-3*bcsamp -> fragility caution); the bycoh comment at 13838-13842 ('it is the same relative tolerance the ccref screen uses, so the two move together by construction'). test_amescreen B2 pins the bycoh band; nothing pins ccref in that band.
findings.proposed_change: Add the same (1e-5, 1e-3) band to the ccref loop, tagging the groups per type as the refusal arm already does, and print a caution of the author's wording naming the type and group count. Blast radius: a caution on runs that complete today with no message; no number moves. Test: a ccref twin of B2.

findings.title: Guide sec 12 says the permute() subgroup screens downgrade to cautions under safety(off); S3 is unliftable and W2 is skipped with no caution
findings.claim: Two sentences in the guide's safety() chapter list, among 'refuses, and safety(off) downgrades to a caution', the two permute() design-population screens (within-cell and split-unit). In the code the permctl split-unit screen S3 refuses at both settings (ruled 2026-09-21, pinned by test_sgsplit G5) and the permctl within-cell screen W2 has no else arm - under safety(off) it is skipped outright and prints nothing. The guide's own messages chapter (1195) shows S3's error with no escape clause, so the chapter contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: wooldid_agent_guide.md 729 ('the subgroup containment screens, with or without permute(): the within-cell screen is skipped outright and the split-unit screen becomes a caution') and 749 ('under permute() with subgroups(), the two design-population screens ... [refuses, and safety(off) downgrades to a caution]'); wooldid_permctl 6497-6509 (W2: if _rc != 0 & si != off -> error, no else) and 6511-6530 (S3: unconditional error 459, comment 'UNLIFTABLE by safety(off), ruled by the author 2026-09-21'); test/test_sgsplit.do G5 asserts 459 at both settings.
findings.proposed_change: Move S3 to the 'refusals that stand whatever safety() is set to' list and describe W2 as skipped under safety(off); documentation only.

findings.title: W1 and S1 run inside every bootstrap and permute replication while S2 is replication-gated; f8b4a64's argument applies to them too
findings.claim: wooldid_sgdom's partial-labelling guard S2 is gated on rm != 1 with the reasoning that the observed run's screen is the one that matters and the assert then costs nothing per replication; the two guards above it, W1 and S1, carry no such gate and re-run their four gegen passes and two asserts in every nested call. They cannot newly fail there: bootstrap re-id rebuilds i finer than the original (containment within the new i follows from containment within the old), reweighting keeps rows and labels together, and permute's W2/S3 already verified every unit of the design population. Commit f8b4a64 gated the onset-constancy and maxvar checks on exactly this argument.
findings.evidence: wooldid_sgdom 13033-13073 (no rm test) vs 13102 (if rm != 1 on S2); the worker passes rm(`wdrepmode') at 1057; wdrepmode is read from the WOOLDID_REPMODE global at 596 that both engines set; both engines emit subgroups() into the replication option string (wooldid 162, 386). Cost measured in Stata P5 (s1_probes.log 19735): the W1+S1 block takes 0.086 s per call on 200,000 rows (4,000 i x 50 t), i.e. about 86 s at reps(999) - the same order as the 5.3 percent share f8b4a64 removed. commit f8b4a64 body (git show).
findings.proposed_change: Wrap W1 and S1 in the same if rm != 1 gate S2 uses (the c_local sglist and the name-length caution stay outside it). Blast radius: replication calls with subgroups() only; no number moves and no replication can newly pass that would have failed.

findings.title: The subgroup name-length caution states its remedy twice in two consecutive lines
findings.claim: The name-length caution prints two lines; the first already ends with the remedy 'recode the subgroup variable to small integers first (egen newsg = group(oldsg))' and the second line repeats it ('If wooldid crashes, recode ID-style subgroup values to small integers first (e.g., egen newsg = group(oldsg))'). The first line also carries mechanism detail (which name prefixes overflow, the factor-variable level cap) beyond condition, consequence and remedy. Reported as a burden only; no wording proposed.
findings.evidence: wooldid_sgdom 13146-13147 (two dis as text lines under the same if). Not among the six cautions the author rewrote on 2026-09-21 (no 'trimmed' marker at the site).
findings.proposed_change: Author's call on the text; structurally, one line carries the condition, the consequence (r(198) on some option combinations) and the single remedy. No number moves.

findings.title: amescreen mode ccref parses and receives ccrwithin() but never reads it
findings.claim: The ccref mode's syntax declares ccrwithin(string) and the worker passes ccrwithin(`contreatwithin'), but no line of the mode's body references the local. The mode's header states that contreatwithin does not rescue the misspecification, so the screen deliberately ignores it - the option is a leftover of a carve-out that was decided against. Harmless, but it invites a reader to look for a contreatwithin branch that does not exist.
findings.evidence: wooldid_amescreen 13702 (syntax ... ccrwithin(string)); wooldid_worker 1507 (ccrwithin(`contreatwithin')); grep of 13724-13831 finds no read of the local.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the option from the syntax line and the argument from the call. Blast radius: none; no number moves.

findings.title: Help and guide say the reference-pool screens name the failing group; the rewritten errors no longer do
findings.claim: The help's contreatcontrols passage says 'A group without it is named and the run stops', and the guide's byCohort entry says 'a cohort that does not is named and the run stops'. The author's 2026-09-21 rewrite of the ccref and bycoh errors dropped the names: the basic/byTreated/byTtre/byTime texts say 'at least one treatment onset group' or 'at least one period', and the byCohort text says 'at least one treated cohort'. The old detail (the cohort number, the byTime period list) is now computed but only kept in comments. The doc claim is the stale side; whether to restore the name in the message is the author's call on his own text.
findings.evidence: wooldid.sthlp 747; wooldid_agent_guide.md 575; wooldid_amescreen 13816-13822 (ccref errors) and 13857 (bycoh error); bcmin still computed at 13840-13849 and ccrlist at 13791-13793.
findings.proposed_change: Either the two doc sentences stop claiming the group is named, or the messages regain the computed name - the latter is message wording and the author's. No number moves.

findings.title: Five uncovered paths in this unit's cert tests
findings.claim: (1) test_amescreen has no one-row-cell arm - A4 (refA.dta, cmix) is multi-row partial containment - so finding 1's false positive is unpinned in either direction. (2) test_sgsplit's five legs are all time splits (sg flips at t >= 6); nothing pins the within-cell guard W1 or its safety(off) fall-through. (3) No cert test or suite config exercises S2, the partial-labelling guard, on either its error or its caution arm (sg_missif blanks whole units). (4) test_valdomains D2 asserts only rc 0 for contreatwithin; nothing pins whether the dose-slope screen runs under contreatwithin, and test_amescreen A5 scans only the worker's vzero text, so the double caution of finding 3 is invisible to the suite. (5) test_amescreen B2 pins the byCohort fragility band; nothing pins the reference-pool screens for the other types in that band.
findings.evidence: test/test_amescreen.do A1-A10, B1-B3, C1-C2; test/test_sgsplit.do G1-G5 (mksplit: sg flipped for i == 3 & t >= 6); grep of test/*.do and test/suite/ for the S2 texts finds nothing; test/test_valdomains.do D2; test/test_amescreen.do A5 scana5 needle.
findings.proposed_change: Add a one-row-cell arm (the P1-A/P1-B pair, expected values per the ruling on finding 1), a within-cell sg arm at both safety settings, an S2 arm (a unit labelled post-onset only, error under default, caution under safety(off)), a contreatwithin twin of C1, and a ccref twin of B2. Test files only.

U11_screens.works_fine: Examined and found sound on the pinned sha. wooldid_ccscreen: the token parse (o./0b./_i/_t/1.targetflag conditions, the duplicate-token check, the problem_i/problem_t extraction and the _t -> relative-horizon conversion at 12684) is byte-equivalent to v1.3 1200-1280; the strpos(bvars, "o.") skip at 12592 only omits a loop that provably cannot fire, and the per-token full-data count gate at 12633 only skips counts whose display v1.3 already gated on lattice/verbose, so the retained collinearity screen is observationally equivalent to v1.3 and owes no ledger row. The untreatedZero refusal (12659-12672) and the amevoid scan (12747-12762) match c.<uservar> because the dose is injected as c.`contreat' at 1174/1364 (verified); the poisson separation branch (12689-12694) counts on esamp as intended; the amevoid domain on targetflag==1 exempts untreatedZero's zero-dose reference periods (test_amescreen C2 passes and reads correctly). wooldid_icscreen: the k-th name maps to the k-th demeaned tempvar because interlist is built in user order (1209-1214). wooldid_sgdom: the negative/integer domains (VAL-G15A, strictly looser than v1.3's raw assert at v13 389-395; test_sgdomain S1-S6) and the sglist domain are consistent; the partial-labelling guard S2 reads _t != 0 with f13sgimin reused as designed, and a unit labelled only on its reference row is refused (P3) with a remedy that fits, so that was not shipped as a finding; permonsetcohorts + subgroups() is refused at permctl 6430, so S1 cannot fire on a rebuilt i inside a replication; the permctl twins W2/S3 use the same cond() missing-fold on the design sample. wooldid_amescreen: ccref screens every requested type with a relative tolerance and puts never-treated in their own byTtre group; bycoh's bctr/bcref/bchas logic and its 1e-5/1e-3 bands behave as test_amescreen B1/B2/B2b pin; sescan is correctly gated off scrubbed and fastnose runs; vzero's relative floor with the editmissing fallback collapses to the exact-zero test when e(b) is absent; detect's any-cell rule is right on multi-row partial containment (A4) and on cluster-at-i designs (P4, 240 cells). The worker's gteffects containment count (2007-2048) is a disclosure-only sibling with no scrub, and its one-row semantics are correct for the cell's own SE. Call-site gating: sgdom runs after wooldid_reltime (869 vs 1057) so _t exists; bycoh/ccref are pre-estimation on ifstatement; detect excludes impvalues/unconditionalse/fastnose as its header states; the ccscreen gate on the working safety value is documented in guide sec 12 (finding 2 argues the documented choice is wrong for two of its members, not that code and docs disagree). No v1.3 regression found in this unit: the only v1.3 analogues are the collinearity scan and the negative-sg assert, and neither changed observably.
