findings.title: A withheld across-subgroup equality test prints as 'p-value for joint test that all SGs have the same att: .'
findings.claim: wooldid_sgdeg withholds the equality test by storing e(joint_<item>_allsgssame) = . (11982-11985) and its caution says the test is 'reported as absent', but wooldid_display gates the line on the STRING of the e() scalar, which is '.' for a missing value, so the line prints with a bare dot on every analytic path where the screen fired. The bootstrap and permute engines post a withheld test the same way - wooldid_bootjnt 7554, 7586, 7644, 7654 and wooldid_permjnt 9049 each 'ereturn scalar joint_<pre><item>_allsgssame = .' on absence - so the string gate passes and the same bare dot prints under either engine whenever its equality test is withheld (code-read; the engine runs here all produced numbers). BS-30 (d9280e7) fixed this exact pattern for the adversarial lines by gating on the numeric value; the equality lines were left on the string gate.
findings.evidence: l1_live.txt:294-297 (dta_binary att att_it cluster(i) subgroups(sg) ...): four lines ending ': .'; l2_clus.txt:173-174 (3-level subgroup), l3_cont.txt:225-226 (contreat), l8_pois.txt:207-208 (poisson) show the same. Engine posts of the missing scalar: pinned 7554, 7586, 7644, 7654 (bootjnt), 9049 (permjnt).

findings.title: The p = 0 resolution line and both bootstrap footer sentences print 'p < 0.000' once completed replications exceed 4000
findings.claim: wooldid_pfloor prints the resolution with %5.3f, and the bootstrap footer prints 2/n and 2/(n+1) with the same format. 2/n falls below 0.0005 at n > 4000 and 1/n (the permrawp resolution) at n > 2000, so an ordinary final run at reps(4999) or reps(9999) prints 'p = 0 above means p < 0.000 (2/4999 completed replications ...)' and 'have resolution 2/4999 = 0.000'. The parenthetical rescues the reader, but the headline inequality is false-looking and the footer's '= 0.000' is wrong as written. The only test of the line (G30) sits at reps(10).
findings.evidence: u10_run1.log: 'L7_fmt_5000=0.000', 'L7_fmt_4000=0.001', 'L7_fmt_1p5000=0.000' (dis %5.3f 2/5000, 2/4000, 1/5000). Live text at reps 12: l4_live.txt:57 'p = 0 above means p < 0.167 (2/12 ...'; footer l4_live.norm 'have resolution 2/12 = 0.167'.
findings.proposed_change: Print the resolution with a general format at the three sites (e.g. %9.0g, or string(x, "%9.2g")), so 2/4999 prints .0004 and 2/10 prints .2. Blast radius: display only; test_bootstrap_gates.do:878 (G30b) anchors 'p < 0.200 (2/10 completed replications' and must follow the new rendering; test_permute3 Q28 anchors only 'p = 0 above means p <' and is untouched.

findings.title: Under bootdisplay(bc)/(bca) the resolution line and the footer describe the displayed p as 'rank-based' with resolution 2/n
findings.claim: wooldid_pfloor fires for every non-wald bootstrap display and its annotation says '(2/n ..., the resolution of the rank-based p)'; the footer's else-branch prints 'The rank-based coefficient p-values have resolution 2/n'. findings.title: ccref screen refuses byTreated/byTtre whenever the never-treated group has a zero or constant dose, though that group's baseline slope is inert
findings.claim: wooldid_amescreen mode(ccref) screens the never-treated group under byTreated (ccrby = ttre==.) and byTtre (missing onset = its own gegen group) and refuses r(459) with no safety(off) escape when its reference-pool dose sd is below 1e-5 of the sample sd. That group's ringer column (i.never#c.ringer) is identically zero when the dose is 0, or in the span of the absorbed cohort intercepts when it is constant, so no treated-cell term is affected; the sibling bycoh mode already screens treated cohorts only (bctr = tvar < .). The help itself tells users to set the dose to 0 off treatment, so the recommended encoding plus the natural control type is refused; v1.3 ran it.
findings.evidence: d_bt (never-treated dose 0, treated unit-constant dose, truth ame 1.0): HEAD byTreated r(459), byTtre r(459) (t_head.log H1a/H1b); v1.3 byTreated rc 0 ame 1.00829723084741 se .0111278, byTtre ame 1.0015383118166 (t_v13.log V1a/V1b); the v1.3 regression omits only o.dose_u (the pooled main effect, the intended drop) and the base-cell co.dose_u term, with all 26 treated dose slopes live (t_v13b.log V6reg_*). HEAD on the same data with a unit-constant jitter of relative sd 1e-3 on the never-treated dose passes the screen and returns ame 1.00829723084742 (byTreated) and 1.0015383118166 (byTtre) with the identical omitted/live structure (ame values from t_head.log H1c/H1d; regression term structure from t_headb.log H6reg_*, read after est restore ___wooldidfullmodel - the N_OMITTED=0 of 12 lines under H1c/H1d in t_head.log are wooldid's posted e(b), not the regression). Every arm on both builds returned the identical att 2.60363242519605, so the control type touches only the ame reference slope. FIX2_FINAL.md claims 0 false positives but its byTreated/byTtre fixtures all carry never-treated dose variation (RULINGS_LEDGER R11 follow-up table).
findings.site: wooldid_amescreen mode(ccref), wooldid.ado 13769 (byTreated ccrby = ttre==.), 13770 (byTtre ccrby = ttre, missing = its own group), 13778 and 13781 (the count/tag over every by-group); bycoh twin 13818 (bctr = tvar < .); help wooldid.sthlp 745-748; guide section 9 decision rule 1
findings.proposed_change: In wooldid_amescreen mode(ccref), for the byTreated and byTtre arms ONLY, build ccrby with the missing-onset rows excluded before the gegen (byTreated: ccrby = 1 if tvar < ., missing otherwise; byTtre: gen ccrby = tvar if tvar < . so gegen skips the never-treated rows), so the never-treated group never enters the sd/count and the tag at 13781 cannot fire on it. Do NOT add a blanket tvar < . to the shared count/tag at 13778/13781: under byTime a post-last-onset period's reference pool is never-treated rows alone and that is FIX-2's true positive, and under basic the pooled slope is identified from the whole pool. Update help 745-748 ('each treatment-status group', 'each onset group') and the guide to say each TREATED group. Blast radius: only runs that today refuse solely on the never-treated group start running; every run that runs today is byte-identical; the suite's byTreated/byTtre configs (never-treated dose varies) are unaffected. Cost: none.

findings.title: A cohort-constant dose is voided-and-continued under basic but hard-refused r(322) under untreatedZero, against the help's unqualified promise
findings.claim: help 662-665 and guide rule 5 promise that when the dose carries no identifying variation for any treated cell's slope (a dose constant within each cohort) wooldid names it, reports the ame as missing and continues with the att. That is what basic does (SI-A4/R6 amevoid). Under untreatedZero the same state-level-intensity design dies r(322) 'a treated cohort-period dummy coefficient was dropped' because the engine drops the cell dummies and keeps the collinear slopes; the att is still identified (dydx(targetflag) toggles the slope term) but the finished regression is thrown away. v1.3 also refuses, so this is not a regression, but the two siblings disagree and the help does not qualify the promise. DEF-2 (R5) covers a dropped dose slope; the dummy-drop path is the older screen.

findings.title: The cell-containment remedy 'bootstrap()' gives the ame rows no inference under boottstat
findings.claim: Under cell containment the ame se/t/p/ci are scrubbed to missing (AMESE R1) and help 802-806 plus the containment caution name bootstrap() as the remedy. Under boottstat the studentization divides by the observed analytic se, which is missing, so the ame rows come back with p and interval missing and a caution that they had no usable studentized distribution; only the non-studentized bootstrap serves them. Neither the containment paragraph nor the boottstat paragraph (394-401) says so.

findings.title: bootstrap() keeps cfxplotnose's one-column cfx shape, so the plot cells get no bootstrap inference while permute() carves it out
findings.claim: D-1 (2026-09-11) gave permute() the fastnose-style carve-out so cfxplotnose no longer truncates the cfx matrices and the cells are rewired from the replications. The gate is written for permute only, so under bootstrap() the matrices stay one column wide and wooldid_bootcellsx skips them silently (colsof < 6 -> continue). The help (360) and guide document the asymmetry rather than close it, although the fix is the same one-token change and costs nothing: the observed margins call still runs nose, the replications already run fastnose, and the rewiring fills the missing-padded columns.

findings.title: Taking the vzero caution's bootstrap() remedy on a lattice run leaves no e(V) (rc 503) for test/lincom/honestdid
findings.claim: On a contreat()+lattice() run whose analytic VCE is all zero, the vzero caution names bootstrap() and permute() as the alternatives that do not use that matrix. Taking bootstrap() gives bootstrap tables, but the worker had posted b-only (no e(V)), and wooldid_bootwire's ereturn repost of the bootstrap covariance to e(V) fails with a conformability r(503); the covariance is kept as e(V_boot) under a caution, so test, lincom, coefplot and honestdid have no e(V) on exactly the design the remedy was recommended for. Engine-generic (any b-only analytic post), observed here on the lattice path.
findings.evidence: t_headb.log H7 (lattice(latv) makecfxplots robust bootstrap(standard) reps(10) on d_bt): 'Caution: standard errors were not identified for 8 of 8 reported estimates, so no variance-covariance matrix e(V) was posted' followed by 'Caution: the bootstrap covariance could not be posted to e(V) (rc 503); it remains available as e(V_boot)'; the vzero remedy text at wooldid_amescreen 13967 ('Bootstrap SEs and randomization inference (permute()) do not use this matrix').
findings.site: wooldid_bootwire wooldid.ado 10740-10764 (the e(V) repost and its rc 503 caution) against the worker's b-only post at 2336-2337 and the vzero unclustered remedy text at wooldid_amescreen 13967
findings.proposed_change: When the analytic post is b-only, have wooldid_bootwire repost b and the bootstrap V together (a full ereturn post/repost carrying V rather than replacing a matrix that is absent). Blast radius: bootstrap runs whose analytic VCE was withheld; today those runs have no e(V), so nothing reported moves. Handoff to the bootstrap-unit reviewer if kept out of this unit.

findings.title: untreatedZero on the poisson/unconditionalse/customvce engines (Form B) has no suite config, so the v1.3 defect it fixed is unpinned
findings.claim: 1c09efa (R5) clears the three ringer inserters inside the untreatedZero branch because v1.3 absorbed a pooled ringer under ppmlhdfe (and carried it as an explicit regressor under unconditionalse/customvce), partialling out the pooled slope that untreatedZero exists to exclude. The suite's untreatedZero configs (cont_uz, cont_uz_ss, ext_cont_ext_untreatedzero, ext_val_untreatedzero_combo) are all on the reghdfe path, so the ledger has no row for this class and a regression of Form B would not be seen by oldnew or the battery.

findings.title: summarystats under untreatedZero omits the pre-treatment and control-group dose rows, the one check of the always-zero premise
findings.claim: B5 (4979abf) fixed an r(198) under untreatedZero + summarystats by not computing the c_pretreat and c_control rows at all. Those rows are well defined and are exactly the diagnostic the option needs: they should be all zeros when the premise holds and the help warns that a violated premise gives poorly identified estimates with no other signal. The guide documents the omission.
findings.evidence: wooldid_sumstat wooldid.ado 13340 and 13366 (the != untreatedZero gates on the pre and control computations), 13389 and 13391 (the row appends); help 511-513; guide summarystats entry.
findings.proposed_change: Compute and post the two rows under untreatedZero as under every other type (four gates removed). Adds rows to e(summarystats) on cont_uz_ss-class runs, so that config needs a ledger row; no existing number moves.

findings.title: The cell-collapse skip caution explains mechanism and measurements on every lattice()/makecfxplots/contreatpoly run while saying no answer changes
findings.claim: wooldid_validate prints, on every run with lattice(), makecfxplots, contreatpoly(>1), interactivecontrols(), unconditionalse, customvce() or the dose inside a control, a caution that states the collapse does not apply and 'no answer changes', then two to five further lines on how the collapse works, why each option breaks it, a measured magnitude ('the ame rows move by up to 0.6 percent') and a note that customvce() is 'held out pending measurement'. The condition and remedy (nofastcollapse silences it) fit in one line; the rest is help text a performance-only disclosure does not need, and it prints ahead of every other message in a lattice run.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 5467-5475 (the dis block) and its trigger 5416-5466; t_head.log H3d prints the four-line form at the top of a lattice run.
findings.proposed_change: Report only: the author writes messages. The candidate is to keep the first line and drop the mechanism lines, or demote the disclosure to verbose. No number moves.

findings.title: Under poisson the cfx and histogram titles call dyex a semi-elasticity, which the help says is the elasticity there
findings.claim: Ceffecttype is 'Semi-elasticities (dyex)' whenever contreatelasticitytype(dyex) is given and 'Effects' otherwise, regardless of poisson. Help 667-670 says that under poisson dydx already gives the semi-elasticity of E[y] and dyex the elasticity, so poisson+dyex plots are titled semi-elasticities for an elasticity and poisson+dydx plots are titled effects for a semi-elasticity. Cosmetic, but the titles are what a user pastes into a paper.
findings.evidence: wooldid.ado 2191-2192 (local Ceffecttype), 2715/2807/2823 (cfx titles) and wooldid_hist 13237/13270 (xtitle); help wooldid.sthlp 667-670.
findings.site: wooldid_worker wooldid.ado 2191-2192 (Ceffecttype); cfx titles 2715-2823; wooldid_hist 13237 and 13270
findings.proposed_change: Make Ceffecttype poisson-aware (dydx -> 'Semi-elasticities', dyex -> 'Elasticities' under poisson). Titles only.

The fast-collapse gate list matches help 291-292 and the guide; wooldid_fcol's contreat handling (i joins the key, dose and ringer replaced by the cell weighted mean under the first estimand weight) is exact because every estimand weight is proportional within an (i,t) cell, and dyex/poisson stay linear in the dose. U12_plots.unit: U12 plots: event study, cfx, saveplots (wooldid_cfxplots, wooldid_esplots, wooldid_esbandv, the worker cfx block, the shell plot dispatch, validate's cfx screens, permcellsx/bootcellsx cell rewiring) on 8965f20

findings.title: permute() + permtstat + cfxplotnose leaves every cfx cell's inference blank with no message
findings.claim: The cfxplotnose carve-out keeps the six-column cfx shape under permute() so the cell rewiring can fill p/ll/ul, and the guide says a permute() run with cfxplotnose 'still gets permutation inference on the plot cells'. Under permtstat that is not what happens: the studentized rewiring divides each cell by its observed analytic standard error and each replication's cell standard error, both of which cfxplotnose suppresses (the option is also forwarded to the replications), so wooldid_permcellwire skips every cell. The posted e(cfx*) matrices carry b alone with se, t, p, ll and ul missing; ndone still counts the matrix, so neither the drift caution nor e(perm_cfx_blank) fires, and the figures and <stem>_cfx.dta are point-only under a randomization-inference header with nothing said.
findings.evidence: mata wooldid_permcellwire 17624-17632: `so = CS[1, k]; if (so >= . | so <= 0 | C[1, k] >= .) continue'; shell 159 forwards cfxplotnose to the replications so S[r,k] is missing too; wooldid_permcellsx 9260-9276 counts the matrix (colsof == 6) and never tests for an all-missing fill. u12_h3.log D1 (Q33 fixture, permute(shuffle) permreps(20) permtstat cfxplotnose): e(cfxatt_cfxpost) = b column only, e(perm_cfx_blank) empty, no caution; D3 (same without permtstat) fills p/ll/ul.
findings.site: wooldid_permcellsx 9260-9276 (skip test), Mata wooldid_permcellwire 17629-17630, shell 159; guide line 563
findings.proposed_change: Handle rather than refuse: under permtstat the observed run already computes standard errors for every coefficient row, so let wooldid_validate clear cfxplotnose when permtstat (or permtci) is in force - one line beside the permtci-implies-permtstat resolution at 5283 - so both the observed cfx margins (worker 2691) and the replication string (shell 159) carry standard errors and the studentized fill proceeds. Blast radius: the permute()+permtstat+cfxplotnose combination only; the cfx cells go from blank to filled (a number moves on a run that currently completes). Alternatively fix the guide sentence and have permcellsx post e(perm_cfx_blank) when a rewired matrix comes back all-missing.

findings.title: saveplots() is the one saver with no pre-check: a stale file is found after the replications and the run is lost
findings.claim: permsave() and bootsave() confirm their file before a single replication runs and refuse with r(602) if it exists without replace. saveplots() has no such check on any path, and what happens then depends on which of its files is stale: on the analytic path a stale <stem>_cfx.dta is a caution and the run completes, a stale ES .gph errors after the tables, and a stale cfx .gph errors inside the estimand loop before any table; under permute() or bootstrap() every one of them - including <stem>_cfx.dta, whose analytic twin is caution-and-continue - surfaces only after all replications, as an r(602) from an uncapped graph save or save, so part(2) and the engine footer never print and the replay branch refuses until another call completes. The help and guide describe the pre-check for permsave()/bootsave() and say nothing about saveplots() being fatal at the end of an engine run.
findings.evidence: Pre-checks: wooldid_permctl 6227-6231, wooldid_bootctl 6706-6710. Uncapped writes: wooldid_cfxplots 14103 (graph save) and 14120 (qui save _cfx.dta), wooldid_esplots 14297/14310/14411/14419, worker 2748/2792 (marginsplot graph save during the loop). Shell 277-289/298-309 (permute) and 528-540/548-559 (bootstrap) exit on the plot rc after the reps. Runs: u12_h4.log F1 (stale cfx .gph, analytic: r(602), no 'Main Results'), F3 (stale _cfx.dta, analytic: caution, rc 0, replay ok), H1 (stale _cfx.dta, permute: 'Main Results' printed, perm_completed=20, then 'file f1_cfx.dta already exists' r(602), replay refused r(198)); u12_h5.log G2 (stale ES .gph, analytic: tables then r(602)), G3 (permute: part(1), 20 reps, r(602), replay refused); test_bootstrap_gates G20 pins the bootstrap ES .gph case as ruled behaviour (2026-09-05); help 508 and guide 79 document the pre-check for permsave()/bootsave() only. The shell comment at 573-580 states the reason the engine branches were left fatal: 'the same call also draws the figures'; capturing only the final _cfx.dta save leaves that reason intact.
findings.site: wooldid_validate (no saveplots file check; syntax 4933) vs wooldid_permctl 6227 / wooldid_bootctl 6706; wooldid_cfxplots 14103-14121; shell 277-309, 528-559
findings.proposed_change: Two small pieces, neither adding number-bearing code. (1) A pre-check placed in the shell AFTER the worker returns and BEFORE the replication loop (not at parse time: <stem>_ES.dta is written only when horizons survive the panel clip and <stem>_cfx.dta only when e(wdid_cfxmats) is non-empty, so a parse-time check would refuse runs that never write the file - the B15 class). Gate it on the shell's existing tests, strpos("`: colfullnames e(b)'", "ES_") > 0 for the ES file and "`e(wdid_cfxmats)'" != "" for the cfx file, and on the engine branches only for _cfx.dta, since the analytic _cfx.dta clash is caution-and-continue by the 2026-09-21 ruling (shell 584); refuse with the r(602) the sibling savers use. Placed there it rejects only calls that would fail after the reps anyway. (2) In wooldid_cfxplots capture the final <stem>_cfx.dta save (14120) and hand its rc back, so the engine branches print the author's existing plot-data caution (shell 584) instead of exiting - the figures and .gph files are already written by then, which keeps the reason stated at shell 573-580. Blast radius: the shell's two engine branches and one save in wooldid_cfxplots; no reported number moves. The error wording for (1) is the author's to write.

findings.title: Engine-path cfx figures lose the user lattice() variable's name and value labels
findings.claim: When the lattice is a one-word user variable (lattice(var), no cfxlattice()), the analytic figure is drawn by marginsplot over that variable, so its x-axis carries the variable name and value labels; under bootstrap() or permute() the same figure is drawn by wooldid_cfxplots from e(), which reads e(wdid_cfxlatvar) and e(wdid_cfxxt) - both empty on this path - so the x-axis is titled 'lattice' with bare integers. The header of wooldid_cfxplots promises 'same names, same titles'. Apart from this the two renderings agree (title, y-title, points, band shape) on a well-behaved fixture.
findings.evidence: worker 4781 posts wdid_cfxlatvar from `cfxlattice' (empty here) not `latticevar' (=`lattice' at 1146); worker 2694-2697 sets cfx_xtitle only for cfxlattice() or a two-word lattice(); u12_harness.log A3/A4: e(wdid_cfxlatvar)=[] e(wdid_cfxxt)=[] on both paths; png_a3_cfxatt_cfxpost.png (analytic marginsplot) shows xtitle 'lat3' with the labels low/mid/high dose, a4_att_bt.png (bootstrap, same spec) shows xtitle 'lattice' ticks 1 2 3; a5_att_bt.png (cfxlattice(lat3)) shows the labels; png_n1/png_n2 (noisy fixture, analytic vs bootstrap wald) otherwise identical in layout.
findings.proposed_change: At 4781 post the plot's over() variable when it is a user variable: wdid_cfxlatvar = cfxlattice if given, else `lattice' when wordcount(lattice)==1 (the auto-lattice tempvar stays excluded), and at 2697 add the one-word case to cfx_xtitle so both renderers title the axis with the variable name. Blast radius: two hidden e() macros and the engine-path figures only; no number moves. The structural alternative, which makes the two paths identical by construction, is to render every cfx figure from e() through wooldid_cfxplots on the analytic path as well and drop the marginsplot calls at worker 2745 and 2789; named here, not proposed.

findings.title: Simultaneous band is drawn straight across the reference period under esfixedbaseperiod
findings.claim: wooldid_esbandv fills __wdsblo/__wdsbhi only at banded horizons and draws them with rline; the reference row (esrelativeto) has no band value, and twoway's default cmissing(y) connects the dashed pair across it. On the esfixedbaseperiod figure the dashed band therefore spans the reference period with a non-zero width while the pointwise shading pinches to zero there, showing an interval where none exists.
findings.evidence: wooldid_esbandv 11776-11788 (rline layer, no cmissing(n)); u12_harness.log E1: e(esband_att) has columns pre4 pre3 pre1 post0 post1 (no pre2); e1_att_esf.png shows the dashed pair crossing -2* at about +-0.3 while the shading pinches to 0.
findings.proposed_change: Add cmissing(n) to the rline layer, or set __wdsblo=__wdsbhi=0 on the rownamesvar=="reference" row so the band pinches with the shading. Cosmetic; no stored result moves.

findings.title: wooldid_cfxstripe rejects Stata's combined base+omitted level marker (1bno.) as a 'novel wooldid bug'
findings.claim: The row-name parser accepts 1b., 1bn. and 1o. but not 1bno., which margins emits when the lattice base level is also omitted - the case where every treated cohort-period dose-slope term is dropped (one observation per i-t cell). That design is pathological for contreat() and wooldid already says so with the multicollinearity caution and completes the run; makecfxplots on it then dies r(498) with a message telling the user to report a bug. It only fires when the cfx margins compute standard errors (cfxplotnose and the fast replications pass), which is why test_permute3 Q33 on the same fixture never saw it.
findings.evidence: wooldid_cfxstripe 11459-11462: regexm("`rsub'", "^([0-9]+)(bn|b|o)?\."); u12_h3.log F0/D2/F2/F3 (Q33 fixture, analytic and permute+permtstat): 'wooldid could not parse the CFX matrix row name dose:1bno.__000008 into a lattice level', rc 498; D1/D3 with cfxplotnose rc 0.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the alternation to (bno|bn|b|o)? - one token, blast radius the row-key rename only; the rows already carry missing cells on that design so no number moves. Low under the pathological-data cap, but the message is the one that tells users to file a bug report.

findings.title: wooldid_permcellsx's skip comment describes the pre-carve-out cfxplotnose behaviour
findings.claim: The comment above the six-column test says that under permute() a narrow matrix 'means cfxplotnose', that permute()+cfxplotnose leaves ndone at 0, that the caution never prints and that the cells 'stay analytic under a permutation header with nothing said'. Since D-1 (2026-09-11) the worker keeps the six-column shape under permute() whatever cfxplotnose says, so that branch is unreachable from cfxplotnose; the comment now misdirects a reader toward a silent path that does not exist while the actual silent path (permtstat, first finding) goes unmentioned.
findings.evidence: wooldid_permcellsx 9253-9259 vs wooldid_worker 2670-2679 and the worker's own comment; test_permute3 Q33 asserts colsof == 6 and a filled p under permute()+cfxplotnose; suite config perm_cfxnose (configs.csv 172).
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the comment to say the narrow shape is unreachable under permute() (the worker pads to six columns) and point at the permtstat all-missing fill instead. Comment only.

findings.title: wooldid, update re-triggers the previous run's <stem>_cfx.dta write
findings.claim: The shell's analytic plot-data twin runs after every worker return with rc 0 and keys on e(wdid_cfxsave). wooldid, update exits the worker with rc 0 without touching e(), so if the session's last successful call was an analytic makecfxplots saveplots() run, the update call rewrites <stem>_cfx.dta from the stale e() (silently when that run had replace) or prints the plot-data write-failure caution (when it had not). Not reproduced: update needs network access.
findings.evidence: wooldid_worker 615-619 (net install, then `exit' with e() untouched); shell 581-584 (`if "`e(wdid_cfxsave)'" != "" cap noi wooldid_cfxplots , saveplots(...) dataonly'); the replay branch 26-43 is the only earlier exit and is gated on an empty command line.
findings.proposed_change: Gate the twin on this call having posted the stem: e.g. have the worker c_local a flag when it posts wdid_cfxsave and test that flag in the shell, or have the update branch `ereturn clear' (it prints 'restart Stata' anyway). Blast radius: the update branch only.

findings.title: Guide: a failure during estimation does not leave the previous wooldid e() in place
findings.claim: The guide's replay paragraph says that if a wooldid call fails at the parse or estimation stage, e() still holds the previous successful estimation. Once the stage-1 regression has run, e() holds that regression's post (reghdfe/ppmlhdfe/regress), so any failure between the fit and the ereturn post - the cfx graph-save clash of the saveplots finding is the reachable one in this unit - leaves e(cmd) as the underlying estimator's, and a bare wooldid is then parsed as a new call and refused by validate rather than by the replay marker.
findings.evidence: guide line 909 ('if a wooldid call fails at the parse or estimation stage, e() still holds the previous successful estimation (standard Stata behavior)'); u12_h4.log F1: after the r(602) inside the estimand loop, `wooldid' alone prints 'Error: command line input should feature all of y i t ttre' (validate), i.e. e(cmd) != wooldid, whereas after the post-display failures G2/H1 it prints the replay-marker refusal.
findings.site: wooldid_agent_guide.md line 909; wooldid_worker 2748 (the failure site exercised)
findings.proposed_change: Narrow the sentence to parse-stage failures (before the stage-1 fit); after the fit e() is the estimator's own post until wooldid posts. Doc only.

findings.title: Four plot-scope cautions carry mechanism or example text beyond condition, consequence and remedy
findings.claim: (1) The non-att makecfxplots caution (both branches) is an interpretation lecture ('difficult unless i-t cells (and sometimes cohorts i) are wholly contained within lattice bins') and, under safety(off), states no consequence at all - it fires and the plots are drawn anyway. (2) The permcellsx drift caution explains why assignment-dependent bins have no permutation distribution and then lists the lattice types that do; the operative content is the three blank columns and the analytic se. (3) The bootcellsx bca caution ends in a parenthetical on the delete-one-cluster jackknife. (4) The bootcellsx studentize caution carries a 'for example the ame covariance is withheld under cell containment' clause. The two esband cautions (11722, 11733) are condition/consequence and fine; the two cfxlattice() cautions (5637, 5658) are fine.
findings.evidence: wooldid_validate 5202 and 5205-5206; wooldid_permcellsx 9314; wooldid_bootcellsx 7084 and 7200; none is among the six cautions the author rewrote on 2026-09-21.
findings.proposed_change: Flagged for the author's own rewrite through the review page; no wording proposed. For (1) the safety(off) branch could also simply not fire (the user asked for it), which is a behaviour question for him.

findings.title: saveplots() rejects any directory part because it is parsed as a Stata name
findings.claim: saveplots() is declared SAVEplots(name) in both syntax lines, so saveplots(figs/es) or a stem longer than 32 characters is refused by syntax before validate runs, and every file lands in the working directory. The three writers already quote the stem, so a stem with a directory part would work as-is; permsave()/bootsave() are string options that explicitly reject a directory part with a named error, which is at least a documented refusal. Retained from v1.3; the help and guide document the restriction rather than lift it.
findings.evidence: wooldid_worker 612 and wooldid_validate 4933: SAVEplots(name); writers quote the stem at worker 2748/2792/2841/2881, wooldid_esplots 14297/14310/14411/14419, wooldid_cfxplots 14103/14120, wooldid_hist 13236-13275; help 504-506 ('the argument is a name, not a path'); guide 77.
findings.proposed_change: Change SAVEplots(name) to SAVEplots(string) in both syntax lines (test/check_validate_sync.py keeps them identical) and, if a directory part is still unwanted, refuse it in validate the way permsave() does. Blast radius: parse only; no number moves.

findings.title: What the cert suites do not pin in this unit
findings.claim: No cert test runs makecfxplotsbysg under either engine (the sg cfx matrices, their .gph files and the _cfx.dta rows are unpinned; they worked in my C1 run). No test covers permtstat with cfxplotnose (the silent blank above). No test compares the analytic (marginsplot) figure with the engine (twoway) figure beyond graph names (T12), which is how the x-axis identity loss went unnoticed. The subgroup ES data at level() other than 95 is pinned only for the pooled file (Q8); the sg files were right in my B1 run. No test exercises a stale saveplots() file on the analytic path or under permute() (G20 covers bootstrap only).

findings.title: permute() screens the design population for four subgroup conditions but not partial labelling; replications then share-weight a partially labelled unit silently
findings.claim: The help (431-432) and guide (486) say that under permute() the subgroup screens run over the whole sample because any cluster can be treated in a replication. permctl mirrors the negative, integer, cell-containment and split-unit screens over insmp, but the partial-labelling screen (R16, 2026-09-20) has no twin there. A never-treated unit labelled on some rows and missing on others passes the observed run (f13sgimin is built over ttre != . only) and, in every replication that assigns it an onset, wooldid_sgdom runs with rm(1) and skips the assert, so that replication enters the unit into its subgroup by its labelled weight share with no message - the very estimand distortion the observed run refuses with r(459).
findings.evidence: probes.log A1-A4: never-treated unit 25 labelled on t<6 only: analytic rc 0 (legal), permute(shuffle) permreps(20) rc 0 with no partial-label caution (A2_partial_caution_seen=0); the same label pattern on a treated unit is r(459) both ways (A3); with WOOLDID_REPMODE=1 and unit 25 given an onset the call runs rc 0 and reports att_i(sg1) = 1.46377617 against 1.59057953 when the unit is fully labelled (A4).

findings.title: safety(off) skips the within-cell screen and prints the over-time caution, which claims att/att_it are unaffected
findings.claim: Within-cell subgroup variation implies within-i variation, so under safety(off) a design whose subgroup varies inside i-by-t cells is never examined by the within-cell screen and instead receives the over-time split caution, whose consequence clause says by-subgroup att and att_it results are unaffected. In the within-cell case that is false: every subgroup reweights the same pooled cell effects, so the by-subgroup att/att_it collapse onto the pooled effect and every contrast is structurally zero, which is exactly why the default-safety error refuses it.
findings.evidence: probes.log B1/B2/B3: i=grp with both subgroups inside every grp x t cell, true effects 1 and 3; default safety rc 459; safety(off) rc 0 with the over-time caution only (says_unaffected=1, withincell_msg=0) and att_sg0 = att_sg1 = att_it_sg0 = att_it_sg1 = 2.020008; the help's remedy egen newi=group(grp sg) gives 1.025783 / 3.014232. Suite record test/suite/out/degeneracy/cautions.csv row fcol_sg (i=cohid, region varies within every cohid x year cell, safety(off)) prints the same caution plus the sgdeg caution for 6 pairwise rows (rho ~ 1 = the shut-down contrasts).
findings.site: wooldid_sgdom 13030-13073 (within-cell screen 13030-13052 wholly inside if safetyinput != off; split-over-time screen 13057-13073 always runs, else-branch caution 13072)
findings.proposed_change: Run the within-cell assert outside the safetyinput gate (one gegen pair already computed) and, under safety(off), print the within-cell condition rather than the over-time one when the within-cell assert fails - i.e. make the over-time caution fire only when the cell assert passed. Bears directly on open_ticket_sgshareweight_2026-09-21.md Q1 (whether the within-cell guards harden): this is evidence that letting them through under safety(off) yields a table whose contrasts are exactly the shut-down ones. findings.title: Fast mode keeps a full delta-method VCE on every binary subgroup-by-horizon margins call (and so does every permute replication) while the contreat twin synthesizes the marker
findings.claim: BS-26 kept the VCE on the binary subgroup-by-horizon call so margins' omission marker survives fast mode. On 2026-09-20 R15 gave the contreat twin a synthesized marker under nose because the real estimability pass is 16-60 s per call and permute() replications run fastnose. The binary side was left on the expensive path, so a fastnose + subgroups() + event-window run, and every permute() replication of one, pays a full VCE per subgroup per estimand family for a marker that the R15 conjunction (zero to 1e-12 and no live treated-cell term for that subgroup-horizon cell) recovers in ~0.05 s.
findings.evidence: probes.log D and probes_patched.log DP on a 300-unit x 12-period panel, 3 subgroups, cluster(i), esprelength(3) espostlength(3), att: fastnose+subgroups 63.67 s, fastnose without subgroups 20.48 s, full run 117.57 s; with line 2239 commented out in a scratch copy the same fast run takes 29.17 s and posts the identical 32-column e(b) (cols_pinned.txt vs cols_patched.txt: COLS_IDENTICAL). A permute(shuffle) permreps(500) run on this design would spend roughly 500 x 34 s in that one call. The identical column set on this design demonstrates the COST only, not the synthesized marker's correctness: the design has no non-estimable subgroup horizon, so nothing was there to be dropped either way.
findings.site: wooldid_worker 2233-2239 (sgmarginsdof df(df_r) under fastnose + subgroups + ES window), 3164 (the binary call that consumes it); contreat twin 3533 and 3560-3660 (R15 synthesized marker under nose)
findings.proposed_change: Port the R15 synthesized-marker block to the binary subgroup-by-horizon site: under nose, condemn a column iff its value is zero to 1e-12 and no cohort in that (subgroup, horizon) cell with nonzero estimand weight has a live 1.targetflag cell term in e(b) (the binary lattice is i._i#i._t#1.targetflag rather than the dose slope), write o. into the colname, and drop the sgmarginsdof carve-out. Blast radius: the observed fastnose run and every permute() replication with subgroups; e(b) values do not change (nose and df() give the same b), only which structural-zero columns are dropped, and only where the conjunction disagrees with margins' verdict - R15 measured 487/487 agreement on the contreat side, and it should be re-measured here (test_si7.do's fixtures are the fixtures). The BS-26 abort at rep 0 (observed vs replication column sets) is the guard that would catch a disagreement. One interaction to state: wooldid_fcdegx returns as soon as r(V) is absent (14572-14574), so under fastnose the horizon call is the only sg call the collapse screen can currently fire on, and removing its VCE makes fcdeg inert on a fast-mode observed run (the reps already run without it); the conjunction's zero-to-1e-12 half is what absorbs the ~1e-16 collapse residue at that site, so the port covers what fcdeg was catching there, but that should be said in the commit rather than discovered.

findings.title: suppresssgprimaryeffects disables the pairwise rank-deficiency screen although the pwcompare pass already computes the level margins it needs
findings.claim: The screen rebuilds the level covariance from the two level standard errors and the contrast se; under suppresssgprimaryeffects the level tables are never posted so every row is skipped and a degenerate contrast (cluster at or above i) is reported with its residue se, t and p, and the allsgssame tests are posted, with no caution - the guide says so. But the same pwcompare(effects) margins that yields the contrasts returns the level margins in r(table) on every run; only the read is gated on suppress. Two hidden per-subgroup se vectors captured off that pass would let the screen run unchanged.

findings.title: Under permute() with permtstat/permanalyticse the degenerate analytic pairwise se is printed as se_analytic with no disclosure; bootstrap boottstat discloses the same number

findings.title: The permute(shuffle)+subgroups() caution names permstrata(sg) as the remedy, which permctl refuses whenever sg is missing on never-treated units
findings.claim: The caution's remedy clause tells the user to pass permstrata(sg). Under the help's own convention the subgroup variable is missing on never-treated units, and permstrata() requires every in-sample cluster to carry a nonmissing stratum, so the remedy as printed is refused with r(459). The guide's rules-of-the-road row carries the missing step (fill sg first); the caution, which is what the user sees, does not. Reported under lens (f): the remedy clause is incomplete rather than wrong; no wording proposed.
findings.evidence: probes.log F1/F2: with sg = . on never-treated units, permute(shuffle) permreps(20) prints the caution (permstrata_remedy_caution=1); adding permstrata(sg) gives r(459) 'permstrata() requires clusters be subsets of strata (with no missing stratum values)'.
findings.site: wooldid_permctl 6533 (the caution) and 6570-6580 (permstrata refuses any missing stratum value); help 625 (missing sg means no subgroup) and guide 476 (adds 'fill sg on every in-sample row first')
findings.proposed_change: Author's wording. The structural alternative is to let permstrata() treat a missing stratum as its own stratum (then never-treated clusters would never draw an onset, which changes the design), so the text fix is the right one.

findings.title: permctl's within-cell screen is gated on safety(off) but the unliftable split screen behind it fires on the same data, so the gate only changes the message

The si gate therefore never lets a within-cell design through; it only selects the less specific message.

Examined and found sound on 8965f20: (1) sgdom domain screens - negative/integer on ifstatement & internal ttre<. / t>=ttre (test_sgdomain S1-S6 semantics hold), the split-over-time refusal with its safety(off) caution, the partial-label screen on treated units including the never-treated admission (probes A1/A3), the name-length caution; consistent with help 623-652 except as filed. (2) wooldid_sgchain reads names back, skips o. columns, suppresses one-term chains; the rank guard defers to contrast(overjoint) exactly as the ledger DDG rows record; the EFF3 deferral is binary-only with the pre-period pwcompare fallback (test_sgdefer D1-D5) and the F1 sgprelist rescue keys on the pre-period count. (4) The escomp subgroup pass, wooldid_vsplice's ES_<base>_SG<sg>_ prefix, and the ereturn block including the sgnopre/why/row triple that wooldid_display reads back for replay. (5) wooldid_sgdeg: polarisation rho with missing-contrast-se counted as degenerate, the 1e-2 cut, blank vs report keyed on the user's safety value, replay via e(wdid_sgdegen*), analytic path only because bootjnt/permwire consume column 2 (test_sgdegen G1-G6). (6) Collapse chain: subgroups in the fcol key; fcsg arms wooldid_fcdeg on every subgroup margins call incl. the one-realized-subgroup level calls; the fcpass rerun un-posts before restore,preserve; the fallback propagates to replications through e(wdid_fcguard) in both shells. (9) The share-weighting mechanism itself is not code (the ticket is right): the estimand weights never branch on the subgroup variable; the by-subgroup att/att_it under an over-time split are row/cell-weighted as the help says (probe B shows the claim fails only in the within-cell case). Ledger rows F1SG-*, SI7-*, DDG-*, C-SGlab-*, BS15-*, SIA4-*, AMESE-R1-sg* account for every subgroup number-mover I could trace to a commit.

U15_docs.unit: U15_docs: help and guide against the code (wooldidinstall/wooldid.sthlp, wooldidinstall/wooldid_agent_guide.md, README.md, wooldid.pkg, stata.toc vs wooldid.ado at 8965f20)

findings.title: Help and guide say fastnose is refused with bootstrap(); the code accepts it with a caution and drops it
findings.claim: The help's fastnose entry (L283) lists bootstrap() among the options fastnose is 'Refused with', the bootstrap() entry (L355) lists fastnose among its refusals, and the guide repeats the refusal at L228, L275, L281, L665 and in the engine-compatibility table (L771: 'refused / it is the default'). On the pinned build only fastnose+boottstat is refused; fastnose with a plain bootstrap() prints a caution, is cleared, and the observed run proceeds on the ordinary bootstrap path with e(V) = V_boot. A user reading either file avoids a working call, and nothing tells them the option is silently dropped rather than honoured.
findings.evidence: wooldid_bootctl 6855-6861: `if "`fn'" != "" { if "`bts'" != "" {error 198} dis as text "Caution: fastnose-style speedup tricks are automatically employed with bootstrap()..." }`; shell 5311-5316: `if "`bootstrap'" != "" & "`fastnose'" != "" & "`boottstat'" == "" local fastnose` (comment: ruled 2026-09-21). Probe T2: `wooldid y i t ttre, att cluster(i) fastnose bootstrap(standard) reps(5) rseed(1)` -> T2_RC=0, e(wdid_vcvstate)=bootstrap, e(properties)=b V; T3 with boottstat -> rc 198. test/test_bootstrap_gates.do 5c pins the code behaviour. The guide's own messages chapter (L976) keys this caution on `"`bts'" != ""`, the inverse of the guarding condition (fn != "" & bts == ""), so a reader following ch14 concludes the caution fires WITH boottstat.
findings.site: wooldid.sthlp L283 and L355; wooldid_agent_guide.md L228, L275, L281, L665, L771; code wooldid_bootctl 6855-6861, wooldid (shell) 5316
findings.proposed_change: In the help's fastnose and bootstrap() entries and the guide's five sites, replace 'refused with bootstrap()' by: accepted without boottstat, cautioned and dropped (the observed run and replications are already fast where they can be), refused only with boottstat. Blast radius: documentation only; no number moves.

findings.title: Help and guide say fastnose is refused with impvalues; the code cautions and clears it
findings.claim: The help's fastnose entry (L283) lists impvalues among the refusals and the impvalues entry (L277) says IM inference 'is not allowed with ... fastnose'; the guide's fastnose entry (L228, L665) says 'each is refused with an error'. The code prints 'Caution: fastnose is unnecessary with impvalues...' and clears the option, and the run is byte-identical to a plain impvalues run. The guide's own messages chapter (ch14) lists the caution, so the guide contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: wooldid_validate 5729-5732: `if "`impvalues'" != "" { dis as text "Caution: fastnose is unnecessary with impvalues..."  local fastnose }`. Probe T1: `wooldid y i t ttre, att cluster(i) fastnose impvalues` -> T1_RC=0, e(properties)=b V; T13: mreldif(e(wdidmainresults) with and without fastnose) = 0. test/test_fastnose.do T4b pins the code (ruled 2026-09-21).
findings.site: wooldid.sthlp L277 and L283; wooldid_agent_guide.md L228 and L665 (fastnose entries); code wooldid_validate 5729-5732
findings.proposed_change: Remove impvalues from the two help refusal lists and the guide's fastnose entry; say instead that fastnose is redundant under impvalues, cautioned and ignored. Documentation only.

findings.title: Help permute() and two guide sites promise a histogram caution that no longer exists, and call the histogram 'analytic'
findings.claim: The help's permute() entry (L437) says 'The histogramcohorteffects output stays analytic, with a caution', the guide's Supporting Features entry (L75) says a caution prints under both engines, and the guide's bootstrap() block (L281) says the histograms are 'computed from the analytic covariance ... and a caution says so'. The two cautions were deleted on 2026-09-21 and wooldid_hist passes nose on every margins call, so no covariance reaches the histogram and no caution prints. The guide's permute() block (L381) and engine table (L787) state the current behaviour, so the guide contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: wooldid shell 561-569 comment: 'No caution is printed about it, and the two that used to be here and in the permutation block were deleted on 2026-09-21 as factually wrong'; wooldid_hist 13206, 13220, 13251, 13258: every `margins` call carries `nose`; `grep -i histogram wooldid.ado | grep -i caution` returns nothing. Probe T4 (histogramcohorteffects + permute(shuffle) permreps(20)) and T5 (+ bootstrap(standard) reps(5)): rc 0, no histogram-related caution in the log.
findings.site: wooldid.sthlp L437; wooldid_agent_guide.md L75 and L281; code wooldid 561-569, wooldid_hist 13206-13258
findings.proposed_change: Drop 'with a caution' from the help's permute() sentence and align it with the histogramcohorteffects entry (point estimates from the observed fit, no covariance involved); fix guide L75 and L281 to match guide L381/L787. Documentation only.

findings.title: Guide's bootstrap() block says i-named covariates keep their codes and are cautioned; help, guide ch3 and the code re-key them
findings.claim: The guide's bootstrap() 'From the help file' block (L281) says a term naming i inside fe()/controls()/interactivecontrols()/coarsecohortcontrols()/ccc_absorb() 'keeps its original codes across the copies' and that 'wooldid cautions when it sees the bare i variable named'. Since c24ab48 the shell rewrites those terms to the fresh unit code (wooldid_isub) and posts e(boot_covsub); no such caution exists. The help (L360-362) and the guide's own estimands chapter (L193) describe the re-key. A reader of L281 would expect a caution that never comes and would misread e(boot_covsub).
findings.evidence: wooldid_isub 6953-7005 rewrites tokens equal to ivar to the new code; shell 471: `if `wdb_nest' & `wdb_covsub' > 0 ... ereturn scalar boot_covsub`; no 'original codes'/'bare i' caution in the ado (grep). Probe T6: `wooldid y i t ttre, att att_i cluster(state) fe(i) bootstrap(standard) reps(5) rseed(1)` -> e(boot_covsub)=1, e(boot_reid)=1, no caution beyond the reps grid caution.
findings.site: wooldid_agent_guide.md L281 (contrast L193 and wooldid.sthlp L360-362); code wooldid_isub 6953-7005, wooldid 356-362 and 471
findings.proposed_change: Replace the stale sentences at guide L281 with the re-key description already at L193. Documentation only.

findings.title: Guide's nofastcollapse entry enumerates two ineligible conditions and calls itself the complete list; help, guide ch11 and the code have seven
findings.claim: The guide's nofastcollapse entry (L248-250, duplicated verbatim at L685-687) says 'this paragraph is the single place that enumerates' the ineligible requests, lists only interactivecontrols() and the dose variable inside a controls option, and adds 'Everything else is eligible ... contreat() is eligible ... with every flavour of contreatcontrols()'. The code also skips the collapse for contreatpoly(>1), lattice(), makecfxplots, unconditionalse and customvce(), which the help (L289-291) and the guide's own performance rules (L657) and runtime section (L703) list. The ~10 KB cell-collapse block is also present twice in the guide.
findings.evidence: wooldid_validate 5413-5456: fcbad accumulates contreatpoly(>1), lattice(), makecfxplots, contreat-in-controls, interactivecontrols(), unconditionalse, customvce(); 5466-5474 caution names each. Help L289-291 lists the same seven.
findings.site: wooldid_agent_guide.md L248-250 and L685-687 (block duplicated L214-253 vs L671-736); wooldid.sthlp L289-291 (correct); code wooldid_validate 5413-5456
findings.proposed_change: Make the guide's enumerated list the seven-item one the help carries and remove one of the two copies of the block. Documentation only.

findings.title: The build is stamped version 1.4 / 2026-08-19 in the ado, the help and the pkg, but 401 commits including the bootstrap engine landed after that date
findings.claim: wooldid.ado L2 (`*! version 1.4 2026-08-19`), wooldid.sthlp L2 and wooldid.pkg (`Distribution-Date: 20260819`) agree with each other, but 401 of the 557 commits since v1.3 are dated after 2026-08-19, including bootstrap() and its whole option family (133b11b 2026-08-30 onward), simultaneousbands, permstepdown, permonsetcohorts, the p-value conventions and the guide itself. Stata's adoupdate and SSC's update detection key on Distribution-Date, so a user who installed the 08-19 build would not be offered this build, and a bug report quoting the version line would name a build without bootstrap().
findings.evidence: `awk '$2 > "2026-08-19"' commits_since_main.txt | wc -l` = 401; git log shows wooldid.pkg last changed by b0c58d0 (2026-09-21, added the guide file line) and acd9f7e (2026-08-19, release metadata) without a date bump; the pkg served from GitHub main is still 20240207.
findings.site: wooldid.ado L2; wooldid.sthlp L2; wooldidinstall/wooldid.pkg Distribution-Date line
findings.proposed_change: Bump the version line in the ado and help and the pkg Distribution-Date at release time (or now, to the commit date). Metadata only; no number moves.

findings.title: Guide says per-subgroup joint tests are e() local macros under the replication engines; they are scalars
findings.claim: The guide's Stored Results entry for 'Joint Tests by Subgroup & Time Period' (L871) states the values are e() scalars on an analytic run and e() local macros under bootstrap() and permute(), and tells code that keys on the type to 'expect both'. The pinned code posts scalars in all three cases. Code written to the guide's advice would look in e(macros) and find nothing (harmless if it also checks scalars, misleading otherwise).
findings.evidence: wooldid_bootjnt 7441: `if `jp' < . ereturn scalar `ename'_s`sg' = `jp'   // scalar, not macro`; wooldid_permjnt 9085: `ereturn scalar `ename' = `jp'` with ename = ..._s`sgtag'; grep 'ereturn local joint_' finds nothing. Probe T7 (bootstrap) and T8 (permute) with subgroups(sg) espre(2) espost(2) jointtests: joint_horiz_s1 and joint_att_allsgssame in e(scalars) = 1, in e(macros) = 0.
findings.proposed_change: State that these are scalars under every engine. Documentation only.

findings.title: Guide cites 'the existing caution at fewer than 10 clusters in total', which the code does not have
findings.claim: The guide's bootstrap() block (L281) says the few-treated-clusters caution fires 'beside the existing caution at fewer than 10 clusters in total'. No caution in the ado tests a total cluster count of 10; the only cluster-count cautions are the <6 treated-clusters one (bootrun) and the <6 ever-treated one (permctl).
findings.evidence: `grep -nE '< *10\b' wooldid.ado | grep -i clus` and `grep Caution wooldid.ado | grep -i 'few clusters'` return nothing relevant; wooldid_bootrun 9500 is the only bootstrap cluster-count caution (`r(N) < 6`).
findings.proposed_change: Delete the parenthetical. Documentation only.

findings.title: Guide ch12 says safety(off) suppresses the espostlength-raised caution; the code and the guide's own espostlength entry say it always prints
findings.claim: Guide L753 lists 'the announcement that espostlength was raised' among cautions safety(off) suppresses. The code prints that caution unconditionally and gates only the two advice lines on safety; the guide's espostlength entry (L441) says exactly that. The help (L578, L624) says 'under a caution' without qualification, which is right.
findings.evidence: wooldid_validate 5225-5233: `dis as text "Caution: espostlength set to 1 ..."` unconditional; `if "`safety'" != "off"` guards only the two following lines. Probe T17 (`subgroups(sg) espre(2) safety(off)`): the caution prints.
findings.proposed_change: Move the item from the 'suppresses a caution' bullet to a note that only its advice lines are suppressed. Documentation only.

findings.title: Help says the ccc_absorb() absorption failure stops 'with an error naming this option'; the error names neither ccc_absorb nor any option
findings.claim: The help's ccc_absorb() entry (L874) says that with an event-study window a variable constant within cells absorbs the treatment interactions and 'the run stops with an error naming this option'. The error text was trimmed on 2026-09-21 to 'Check your specified controls and fixed effects.' and no longer names ccc_absorb(). The error wording itself is the author's and out of scope; the help's claim about it is not.
findings.evidence: wooldid_worker 1933: `dis as error "Error: the fitted model carries no estimable treatment-effect coefficient at any of the requested event-study relative periods. Check your specified controls and fixed effects. "` (1936: 'message detail trimmed ... 2026-09-21'). Probe T18 (`espre(2) espost(2) ccc_absorb(ux)` with ux constant within i): rc 459, message as above.
findings.proposed_change: Change 'an error naming this option' to 'an error' (or restore the option name in the message, the author's call). Documentation only.

findings.title: Guide ch14 'prints when' column is extracted at the wrong nesting level for at least three rows, one of them inverted
findings.claim: Chapter 14 tells the reader to 'read the condition to learn what triggered a message you saw'. For at least three rows the column carries the neighbouring `if`, not the guarding one: the bootctl fastnose caution (L976) is keyed on `"`bts'" != ""`, which is the error's condition and the inverse of the caution's; the gteffects 'found no cohort-by-relative-period main-effect coefficients' caution (L951) is keyed on `` `gtprc' == 0 & `gtndegen' > 0 `` although it prints on the `else` of the enclosing block; and the worker's 'adversarial pre-trend testing was skipped due to insufficient event study horizons' caution (L928) is keyed on `"`adversarial'" != ""` alone, dropping the window condition that actually decides it. The chapter is generated (8d3ae94, 8965f20), so the defect is in the extractor and the whole chapter regenerates when it is fixed.
findings.evidence: wooldid_bootctl 6855-6861: caution sits inside `if "`fn'" != ""` after the `bts` error branch; wooldid_worker 4525-4531: the 'found no ...' caution is the `else` of the `if` that contains the gtndegen block; wooldid_worker 1034-1035: the adversarial-skipped caution is guarded by `(espre + espl + 1 < 3 & timetrends) | espl == 0 | espre == 0`. Guide rows at L976, L951, L928.
findings.site: wooldid_agent_guide.md L928, L951, L976 (ch14 table); code wooldid_bootctl 6855-6861, wooldid_worker 1034-1035 and 4525-4531; generator behind commit 8d3ae94
findings.proposed_change: Make the generator record the innermost enclosing `if` chain (including an `else` branch) rather than the nearest preceding condition, then regenerate ch14. Blast radius: the messages chapter only; no number moves.

findings.title: Seven cautions carry mechanism or literature prose that duplicates the help and guide
findings.claim: These cautions in the docs unit's scope explain the mechanism or restate help prose rather than stating condition, consequence and remedy: the cell-collapse skip caution and its per-option lines (validate 5467-5474, including a measured magnitude, duplicating the help's nofastcollapse entry); the >100-values-of-i caution (worker 1477, runtime mechanism and the fe() recipe, duplicating the help's Runtime section); the two cluster-at-i permutation cautions (permctl 295 and 303, exchangeability mechanism duplicating the help's permtstat entry); the bootstrap(bayes) cell-weighted caution (bootctl 6911); the <6 treated clusters caution (bootrun 9500, describes what is implemented and refers to boottest); and the gt_ncontained caution (worker 4522, which refers the reader to a help section by name). Not proposing wording; the author writes every message. bootctl 6911 and bootrun 9500 belong to the engine units and are listed here only because their text duplicates help prose; do not count them twice.
findings.evidence: Line numbers as listed; text visible at those lines and reproduced in the guide's ch14 table.
findings.site: wooldid_validate 5467-5474; wooldid_worker 1477 and 4522; wooldid_permctl 295 and 303; wooldid_bootctl 6911; wooldid_bootrun 9500
findings.proposed_change: Trim each to condition + consequence + remedy and leave the mechanism to the help/guide entry it duplicates; author-written wording. No number moves.

U15_docs.works_fine: Read in full: wooldid.sthlp (1287 lines), wooldid_agent_guide.md (1469 lines), README.md, wooldid.pkg, stata.toc, and the relevant subprograms of the pinned ado. v1.3 analogue: only the help file has one (v1.3 main:wooldidinstall/wooldid.sthlp); the guide, README bootstrap/permute text and the pkg guide line have none. I audited the help against the CODE, not against the v1.3 help (see untested). Sound, by claim: (1) Option surface: every option in the ado syntax line (612) has an {opt} entry in the help and is named in the guide; nothing in the help or guide names an option the code lacks. (2) Stored results: every e() name the help and guide list is posted somewhere in the ado (ereturn_names.txt in the work dir), including the aliases e(boot_percentile_mainresults) and e(perm_lb_*)/e(perm_ub_*), the 13 summarystats scalars (probe T16 counted 13), e(Nclus)+e(N_clust), e(vce)/e(vcetype)/e(vce_stage1), e(level) with lb_90ci/ub_90ci naming under level(90) (T15), e(anticipation), e(escomp*) with its six scalars, the roth_* family, the esband_* family, the perm_stepdown/perm_Cstepdown tables (posted via macro name at 8984, displayed at 12428), e(chi2) missing under ppmlhdfe which the help's 'wherever available' covers (T11). (3) Defaults: dots 1 (7979, 9393), regtol 9, level c(level), esrelativeto -1, contreatpoly 1, bootdf clusters iff cluster() (454), bootdisplay percentile (7078), bootalpha equal (9394), e(perm_pconv) equaltailed (8706), permreps floor 20. (4) Refusals read against the ado and cross-checked against ch14's error table; nine run in Stata: fastnose+boottstat (T3, 198), permute without cluster() (T9, 198 via the wordcount!=1 gate), dots(0) with no engine (T10, 198), espostlength(-999) accepted / other negatives refused, esrelativeto>-1 under esfixedbaseperiod, level() domain 10-99.99 two decimals, pretrendpower levels in (5,100), bootdf integer parse, bca requires cluster(). Also verified in code: impvalues finer-than-i gated on safetyinput (1535-1580), permexact caps 1000/65534 and the 10,000 draw-matrix cap, bootsave/permsave existence checks before replications, oldsyntax refused by both engines, bootalpha only with bayes, boottstat refused with poisson/bayes/wald/bc/bca, unconditionalse/customvce/impvalues single-cluster requirements, contreatcontrols group-variation screens per type (amescreen 13810-13871), byCohort r(459). (5) Cautions that the help says fire and do: jointtests/pretrendpower cluster-at-i screen is a caution not an error (1600-1625; T12 rc 0), >100 values of i, float above 2^24, if-rule count, espostlength raise (T17, also under safety(off)), <6 treated clusters (bootrun 9500), <6 ever-treated clusters (permctl 309), permreps above 10% of assignments, fcskip, cfxlattice missing, anticipation off-grid, all-zero covariance under timetrends+cluster(i), interactivecontrols reduction, cell-containment ame screen, gt_ncontained/gt_ndegen. (6) Cell-collapse eligibility: help and guide ch11 rules match the code's seven-item list. (7) net get: `net describe` on a copy of the package classifies wooldid_agent_guide.md as ANCILLARY (T14), so the help's 'copied to the working directory by net get wooldid' is true. (8) gteffects print cap 200 rows (12363); timer after the fifth replication (8266-8275); update installs from branch main (616); Stata 16 version statements; the pkg's dependency line matches the help. (9) The help's cfxplottypes rule (window screen without esfixedbaseperiod, any integer except the reference with it) matches validate 5556-5560. (10) README: every option it names exists; its omissions are labelled 'Selected Options'.
U15_docs.untested: (1) Lens (b) for the help: I compared the current help against the code, not against the v1.3 help, so what the 2026-09-21 paring removed that was still true is unexamined. (2) Guide prose I did not measure: the timing magnitudes (35-60%, 1.24x/1.25x/1.33x/2.0x, 'about 19 times more', the 1.3rd-1.9th power claims), the collapse precision bounds (2e-15, 1e-13), the honestdid positional-geometry conditions and the empty-confidence-set claim, the bootsave()/permsave() column layouts and dataset characteristics, the if-rule's e(N_dropped) accounting, and `update` end to end (I checked the URL and branch only). (3) e() contents: I verified that every documented name is posted and, for a handful, its type; I did not verify what any matrix holds (column order, row keys, the gteffects weighted-mean identity, escomp column semantics). (5) The README/pkg 'Conley-Taber-spirit' wording vs the guide's 'not the Conley-Taber construction', and README's master-branch install URL vs the ado's main (both resolve via GitHub redirect today), are parked in NOTES.md below the twelve-finding cut. (6) Behaviours neither file states: the WOOLDID_BOOTNOCOVSUB / WOOLDID_BOOTNOSUB / WOOLDID_BOOTDEBUG diagnostic globals are covered only by the guide's 'WOOLDID_* names are reserved'; the cellkeydup and permstrata-advice cautions appear only in ch14, not in help prose. (7) Stata runs were limited to the two probe do-files (18 short configurations on test/data/dta_binary and dta_cont); no poisson-with-subgroups, lattice, or long-replication configurations were run for this unit.

findings.title: Battery pin perm_atti asserts a permreps() refusal, not the att_i-under-permute() run its commit claims
findings.claim: 3ce24d4 (2026-09-16) says perm_atti ("att_i under permute(shuffle)") was measured "rc 0, 20/20" and that it closes the zero-coverage gap for a cell-weighted estimand under permute(). The battery row in test/runbattery.do passes permreps(10) against the engine floor of 20, so the blessed baseline test/baseline/perm_atti.csv is rc|198 with no e() at all, and every battery run since has been "IDENTICAL" to that refusal. findings.title: si20_lat_byt: five unbounded ledger rows and a 1e-2 V bound rest on a df-factor mechanism the degrees-of-freedom fix removed
findings.claim: SI20-L-si20_lat_byt-{wdidmainresults,F,rmse,joint_horiz,joint_Choriz} (unbounded) and SI20-P-si20_lat_byt-V (rtol 1e-2) explain their divergence as "df_r 1263 -> 1258 ... se/t/p/ci move by the df factor (se 2e-3 rel) and p/t tail cells up to 0.15" / "V scales by the df factor 1263/1258 (measured 4.0e-3)". 6fe814d (2026-09-14) removed that over-count; the ledger's own SI20-L-MECHANISM note says df_r is EQUAL on both builds, and cb1796b claimed to rewrite all 105 df-clause rows but touched none of these. U09_ptp_bands|esband-normal-law-vs-t-poi.reason:
Confirmed as a straight bug. At 8965f20, wooldid_esbanda simulates the sup critical value from z ~ N(0,R) and takes no degrees of freedom. The pointwise intervals in the table and on the plot come from margins with df(df_r) (worker line 2213: `local marginsdof df(`df_r')`). Neither the analytic branch of wooldid_esband nor the worker call at line 4635 passes a df. With few clusters the band therefore comes out narrower than the pointwise interval it is supposed to widen. My runs:
- df_r=6, 2 horizons: crit 2.04 against t 2.45, so the band is about 17% narrower.
- df_r=6, 4 horizons: crit 2.27 against t 2.45, so the band is narrower at all four horizons.
- df_r=9: the reviewer's P2 reproduces.
- df_r=30: the band is wider than the pointwise interval, so the gap no longer shows, though coverage under the t law is still slightly short.

This contradicts four things the package states: the help ("covers every horizon of the family at once with that probability"); the guide table ("not calibrated when: none"); the kernel's own header, which says the band is the pointwise interval widened by c/z_level >= 1 and so silently assumes the pointwise interval is a z interval; and the author's B9 ruling recorded in test_esband, which calls a simultaneous band narrower than the pointwise interval beside it "visibly wrong". The only test of this, test_esband B2, compares crit against invnormal, so it cannot catch the defect.

Severity: I lower it to medium. simultaneousbands is opt-in and the band is a stored and plotted display object. Pointwise results, p-values and joint tests are untouched. The damage is large only at small df_r (roughly under 15 clusters), though there it is real: the dashed band sits inside the pointwise shading. Few-cluster DiD is common enough that a high rating is arguable.

Moves numbers: yes. Every analytic simultaneousbands run with a finite df_r gets a larger e(esband_crit_*) and new e(esband_*) endpoints, because a multivariate-t sup quantile is always above the normal one. The change is tiny at large df_r but still visible in the low-order digits. Bootstrap runs, runs without the band and everything else are unchanged. The normal draws are taken first under the per-family seed and the caller's RNG state is restored afterwards, so the extra chi2 draws do not disturb anything outside the band.

Size: about as claimed. The kernel signature gains a df argument, with the chi2 scaling applied when df is finite. wooldid_esband takes a dfr() option (passed only on the analytic branch) and worker 4635 passes df_r. The B2 floor, and B2's independent hand crit, must switch to the t law. The kernel header comment ('c/z_level >= 1') needs rewording, and the analytic e(esband_*) baselines need re-blessing. The multivariate-t construction (max|z| divided by one common sqrt(chi2_df/df) per draw) matches the package's own t(df_r) convention, and with a single horizon it reduces exactly to the t quantile, so the band cannot fall below the pointwise interval except for Monte Carlo noise.
